articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino Praises USMNT's Future Ahead of Exit for Manchester United HC Job
articles.summary: Former United States Men's National Team coach Mauricio Pochettino was optimistic about the USMNT's long-term outlook after leaving his role to become Manchester United's new manager.
articles.body:
Former United States Men's National Team coach Mauricio Pochettino was optimistic about the USMNT's long-term outlook after leaving his role to become Manchester United's new manager.

"There is an amazing future in this country with the national team," Pochettino told reporters on Saturday.

Pochettino and Manchester United finalized his contract on Friday, although he remained with the USMNT for a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal match with Haiti on Saturday. He'll also coach during the team's clash with Haiti on Tuesday before eventually joining his new club.

Pochettino was initially hired as coach of the USMNT in Sept. 2024, compiling a 21-12-2 record during his tenure.

He helped the U.S. squad finish atop its 2026 World Cup group before securing a 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina in the round of 32, representing the team's first knockout round victory since 2002.

The USMNT were eventually eliminated from the World Cup by Belgium in the round of 16.

The next coach of the United States is uncertain, although former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has been linked to the position.

With rising stars such as Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall joining established USMNT contributors including Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun, Pochettino believes that the future of the squad is bright.

articles.title: How Savannah area football teams fared in playoff football action Friday
articles.summary: Here's a look at how Savannah area high school football teams fared with playoff highlights as seven teams advanced to the next round on Friday, Nov. 13.
articles.body:
Six local teams advanced to the second round of the GHSA state playoffs and Bethesda Academy earned a berth in the SCISA State finals for the fourth consecutive season.

Here's a look at how Savannah area teams fared under the lights on Friday night in the state football playoffs.

Host Calvary Day, which entered the playoffs ranked No. 2 among Class 2A-4A Private Schools in the state, despite its No. 9 seed in the PSR rankings, rolled to a shutout win over Westminster.

Quarterback James Mobley IV was 10 of 15 passing for 180 yards and a touchdown, and his backup, freshman Braylon Brown, went 5 of 6 for 22 yards and a score.

Senior Ca'Den Jones continued in his recent run of stellar performances as he ran for 140 yards and three touchdowns on just seven carries.

Senior Jalen Hicks had five receptions for 82 yards and ran for a touchdown. Junior Ty Pinckney had two catches for 36 yards and a score and sophomore Matt Gibson added a touchdown catch.

Linebacker KB Baker III had seven tackles and a pair of sacks and Buddy Curry had a pair of sacks for the Cavs, who improved to 10-1 on the season.

Calvary Day will be on the road to face Greater Atlanta Christian (8-3) on Friday, Nov. 20, in a Class 2A-4A Private second-round matchup.

Savannah Christian 38, Providence Christian 28

Savannah Christian, which entered the playoffs as the No. 21 seed in a 27-team field, went on the road and knocked off No. 12 Providence Christian.

The Raiders got a big-time performance from Cain Tomlin. The senior ran for 148 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries and had two receptions for 60 yards.

Senior Landon Tyson rushed for 112 yards and a score on seven carries and sophomore Wesley Dinkins had 80 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries. Senior William Bucey added a 20-yard scoring run as the Raiders racked up 360 yards rushing ― averaging 9.5 yards per carry.

Junior quarterback Caden Godbee was 8 of 10 passing for 105 yards for the Raiders.

SCPS improved to 6-5 on the season with the victory and will be on the road to face Mt. Vernon (8-2) in a second-round playoff matchup set for Friday, Nov. 20.

The Wildcats went on the road and came away with a hard-fought win over North Paulding as Richmond Hill won its first playoff game since 2020.

CJ Menzie had a strong game for the Wildcats as the workhorse senior rushed for 112 yards and a touchdown on 31 carries.

Senior quarterback Gunner Mobley was 14 of 19 passing for 150 yards and two touchdowns. He connected with DJ Porter and Nick Cameron on scoring passes, while Liberty University-bound senior Eli Grant reeled in seven passes for 90 yards.

Richmond Hill improved to 6-5 on the season with the win and will be on the road to face Brookwood (10-1) in a Class 7A second-round game on Friday, Nov. 20.

The Tigers explosive offense was on display once again as host Bradwell won in a shootout in a Class 6A first round matchup with Dunwoody.

Senior quarterback Jah'Barri Felix was on top of his game once again as he completed 17 of 22 passes for 283 yards and four touchdowns, while rushing for 29 yards on four carries.

Jacobi Pasley, the senior speedster who flipped his commitment from West Virginia to Vanderbilt earlier in the week, had six receptions for 140 yards and a touchdown. Carlito Savea had five catches for 48 yards and two scores. Tyson Spears also had touchdown grab for the Tigers.

Running back Cam Keeve ran for 167 yards and a pair of scores on 18 carries and added a pair of catches for 28 yards.

The Tigers, who are averaging 47 points per game improved to 9-2 on the season under first-year coach John Adams as they won their first playoff game since 2018. It's the first time Bradwell has won nine games in a season since 2004, according to the Georgia High School Football Historians Association.

Bradwell will be on the road to face East Paulding (11-0) in a Class 6A second-round matchup on Friday, Nov. 20.

Sophomore quarterback Liam Coburn was 12 of 23 for 143 yards with a pair of touchdown passes. Calhoun connected with junior Semaj Calhoun twice for 24 yards, with both going for scores. Coburn also ran for a career high of 102 yards with a touchdown on 20 carries.

Khyran White closed out his high school career for the Mustangs with another strong performance as he ran for 103 yards on 20 carries. He finished the season with 1,148 yards rushing and 12 touchdowns.

The Mustangs finished the season with a 7-4 record under Loren Purvis, in his fourth year leading the program. It was the first time South Effingham won seven games in a season since 2015 and the first time the Mustangs reached the playoffs since 2019.

Effingham County lost in the first round of the Class 6A playoffs as visiting Roswell prevailed.

Roswell quarterback Matt Schletty led the way as the senior threw for 265 yards and four touchdowns and ran for 98 yards and a score, according to Donald Heath, who covered the game for the Effingham Herald.

Effingham quarterback Matthew Dillon closed out a stellar sophomore season with a pair of touchdown passes as he finished the year with 27.

Malik Letman had a pick six for the Rebels and Jernard Albright, the senior who has committed to Florida State, had a 97-yard kickoff return for a touchdown.

Senior Jmere Doe-Davis ran for 76 yards on 15 carries and closed out the season with 1,043 yards rushing.

Beach's season came to an end on the road as the Bulldogs lost to Columbia.

The Bulldogs reached the state playoffs for the second year in a row for the first time since the 1990 and 1991 seasons.

Bethesda Academy 43, Hilton Head Christian 14

Bethesda rolled to a win over visiting Hilton Head Christian as the Blazers punched their ticket to the SCISA State finals for the fourth year in a row.

Junior quarterback Jordan Turner led the way as he rushed for 156 yards and two touchdowns on nine carries, while completing 7 of 11 passes for 117 yards and a score.

Jeffrey Armstrong also had a big game as the junior ran for a career-high 159 yards and a pair of touchdowns on 15 carries.

Zhyir Witcher had two receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown for the Blazers, who improved to 9-1 on the season.

Bethesda is up a classification this year playing in SCISA's Class 3A. The Blazers are set to play First Baptist (10-2) in the title game on Saturday, Nov. 21, with kickoff set for 7:30 p.m. at Charleston Southern.

Dennis Knight covers sports for the Savannah Morning News. Contact him at Dknight@savannahnow.com. Twitter: @DennisKnightSMN

articles.title: Watch CFB Fan Make FG in Trending Video After USC Kicker Misses in Loss vs. Indiana
articles.summary: A Hoosiers fan might have added insult to injury after No. 18 USC missed a crucial field goal in a Saturday loss to No. 9 Indiana.
articles.body:
A Hoosiers fan might have added insult to injury after No. 18 USC missed a crucial field goal in a Saturday loss to No. 9 Indiana.

USC kicker Caden Chittenden missed a 27-yard chance to cut the Hoosiers' lead to four points early in the fourth quarter.

An Indiana fan came on the field shortly afterward and successfully kicked a field goal from 35 yards out .

USC never got any closer to completing a Saturday comeback. Quarterback Jayden Maiava threw interceptions on each of the Trojans' next two possessions as his team conceded a 27-13 loss that may have knocked the program out of College Football Playoff contention.

articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC vs. Louisville Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels fell 16-14 to the Louisville Cardinals Saturday, and things got a little chippy after the game.
articles.body:
Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels fell 16-14 to the Louisville Cardinals Saturday, and things got a little chippy after the game.

The Tar Heels entered the matchup as 3.5-point underdogs against the Cardinals who entered with a 6-3 record, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

North Carolina struggled to get its offense going despite playing at home, falling to 5-5 on the season as starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. exited with an injury after a hard hit in the third quarter.

Despite the loss, in his second season as head coach of the Tar Heels, Belichick has already surpassed last season's achievements, when the team finished 4-8.

With two games remaining this season, North Carolina cannot finish below last season's .333 winning percentage. The Tar Heels will hit the road to face the Virginia Cavaliers before closing out the season at home against the NC State Wolfpack.

A big difference has come behind the center. This season, Edwards Jr. has already thrown 18 touchdown passes, surpassing last season's total of 10 by starting quarterback Gio Lopez.

Sophomore running back Demon June has stepped it up this year, rushing for eight touchdowns this season after just two his freshman season with the Tar Heels.

The Tar Heels trailed 13-7 at halftime after taking a 7-3 lead in the first quarter behind a Benjamin Hall rushing touchdown.

A costly fumble by Edwards Jr. in the second quarter gave the Cardinals possession at North Carolina's 21-yard line. Louisville capitalized with a four-play touchdown drive to regain the lead for the first time since opening the game with a field goal.

North Carolina missed a costly 39-yard field goal as both teams went scoreless in the third quarter. Edwards Jr. was sidelined with an injury after taking a sack, forcing freshman Travis Burgess to step in at quarterback.

The Cardinals added a fourth-quarter field goal after North Carolina turned the ball over on downs, extending their lead to 16-7 and making it a two-score game with just under 7:30 remaining.

UNC's Benjamin Hall rushed for a touchdown after a 3:45 drive, cutting the deficit to two points late in the game.

A big stop by the Tar Heels defense gave the offense the ball back just after the two-minute warning, but an interception on fourth down sealed the win for the Cardinals.

The Tar Heels will hit the road to face the Cavaliers next Saturday, with kickoff scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Lincoln Riley Talks USC Hot Seat Buzz, Reiterates He's Right Person for Job After Loss vs. Indiana
articles.summary: USC head coach Lincoln Riley remained steadfast in his belief that he's the right person to lead the Trojans after they suffered a 27-13 loss to Indiana on Saturday.
articles.body:
USC head coach Lincoln Riley remained steadfast in his belief that he's the right person to lead the Trojans after they suffered a 27-13 loss to Indiana on Saturday.

"Absolutely," Riley told reporters after the game. "I believe in what we're doing. I believe in myself. I believe in our leadership. I believe in our administration. I believe in everything what's happening here. Trust me, there's nobody that wants it as bad as all of us involved. We know how close we are as a group, we know how close we are as a team. We got a good view of that tonight. We're gonna keep battling, we will get there and all this will continue to make it more sweet when that time does happen."

Riley previously discussed his commitment to the school after his team secured an upset victory over Ohio State on Oct. 31.

"This win is for all the staff members, the players, the leaders, admin, all the people within the walls," Riley said at the time, via Yahoo Sports' Nick Bromberg . "I said before this game that I'm the right person for this job, and as long as all those people know that, that's all I care about. I appreciate being a part of this university and all it does. I appreciate all our kids and our staff. And I'm going to continue to fight on because that's what being a Trojan is all about."

The Trojans fell to 7-3 with Saturday's loss, effectively extinguishing their College Football Playoff hopes.

USC has posted a 42-21 record since Riley was hired as head coach ahead of the 2022 season, but has yet to clinch a CFP berth. The lack of a playoff appearance has been especially disappointing considering he helped lead Oklahoma to the CFP on three separate occasions during his tenure at the school from 2017-21.

USC will close out its 2026 campaign against Maryland and UCLA.

articles.title: Kenny Dillingham Drops Funny Quote on ASU's Win vs. UCF After Travel Delays From FAA Ground Stop
articles.summary: Arizona State head coach Kenny Dillingham says he wasn't willing to use the chaos of a nationwide ground stop as an "excuse" not to win his team's Saturday matchup against UCF.
articles.body:
Arizona State head coach Kenny Dillingham says he wasn't willing to use the chaos of a nationwide ground stop as an "excuse" not to win his team's Saturday matchup against UCF.

The Sun Devils claimed a 26-13 victory over the Knights Saturday night despite arriving less than four hours before kickoff in Orlando.

"I got told something when I was a high school coach... Excuses are like buttholes. Everybody has them, and they all stink," Dillingham said after the win (h/t 247Sports' Chris Karpman).

Dillingham continued, "That's what tonight would have been. It's just an excuse.

"At the end of the day, you're going to take the field for 60 minutes and play a football game, and you're either gonna get it done or you're not. Nobody's going to care what the circumstance was."

Arizona State was originally scheduled to leave Friday afternoon from Phoenix at 2 p.m. local time before the Federal Aviation Administration grounded planes across the country.

The team then rescheduled the four-hour flight to Saturday around 6 a.m. local time, per the Arizona Republic 's Michelle Gardner and Chris Coppola .

The Big 12 responded by moving Saturday's kickoff in Orlando back two hours to 5:30 p.m. ET.

This marked the latest snag in what has been so far a chaotic schedule for ASU, starting with the Sun Devils traveling to Texas A&M a week before playing Kansas in London this September.

Dillingham's team has played in eight straight weeks since an early bye, and that busy stretch featured two ranked road opponents in Texas Tech and BYU.

ASU will hope for a smoother end to the season as the Sun Devils, which improved to 6-4 with Saturday's win, close out the campaign against visiting No. 25 Oklahoma State and at No. 23 Arizona.

articles.title: Arch Manning, Texas Shock Lane Kiffin, LSU Late, Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns defeated Sam Leavitt, Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers, 22-21, on Saturday after Texas sealed the win with a game-winning drive.
articles.body:
Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns defeated Sam Leavitt, Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers, 22-21, on Saturday after Texas sealed the win with a game-winning drive.

With home-field advantage, LSU entered the matchup as a 4.5-point favorite over Texas, per FanDuel Sportsbook . They lost after a 12-0 second half run from the Longhorns.

Texas improved to 8-2 (5-2 SEC), while LSU fell to 6-4 (3-4 SEC). With an earlier-season win over the Tennessee Volunteers, the Longhorns hold the head-to-head tiebreaker and will move ahead of Tennessee in the SEC standings as they move into third and pursue a potential spot in the SEC Championship Game.

Despite six total turnovers, three interceptions by Leavitt and three by Manning, the game remained exciting down to the wire before the Longhorns sealed it with a game-winning drive as the clock wound down.

Texas and LSU traded touchdown drives on their opening possessions.

Manning ran for a 1-yard touchdown, while Leavitt connected with Jackson Harris for a 10-yard score. Leavitt then threw an interception that was picked off by Texas' Jelani McDonald and both teams were tied at seven a piece headed into the second.

The second quarter was sloppy, with Leavitt throwing his second interception and Manning tossing his first on back-to-back drives.

Leavitt found Harris for his second touchdown of the game to give LSU a seven-point lead before Texas added a field goal to cut the deficit to 14-10. LSU missed a 38-yard field goal to close out the half.

Both quarterbacks traded interceptions on consecutive possessions for the second time in the game to open the second half.

LSU's Dilin Jones rushed for a 44-yard touchdown, while Texas added a field goal as the Tigers extended their lead to 21-13 headed into the fourth.

Manning threw his third interception of the game in the fourth but LSU was unable to capitalize on the other end.

With the game on the line and trailing by five, Texas drove 58 yards downfield, overcoming a near-fumble to secure the road win with a red zone touchdown pass from Manning to Raleek Brown.

LSU will hit the road to face the No. 8 Tennessee Volunteers next Saturday, while Texas will host the Arkansas Razorbacks. Both games are scheduled to kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Arch Manning throws game-winning TD pass with 3 seconds left to crush No. 21 LSU's playoff hopes in No. 6 Texas' 22-21 win
articles.summary: LSU now has four losses.
articles.body:
No. 21 LSU's College Football Playoff hopes got dashed by Arch Manning and Raleek Brown.

No. 6 Texas, meanwhile, is almost assuredly in the 12-team field.

Manning hit Brown on a swing pass with three seconds left for a 4-yard touchdown to give the No. 6 Longhorns a 22-21 win over the No. 21 Tigers.

The TD pass came after Manning ran for a first down inside the LSU 5-yard line with nine seconds to go. The Longhorns had one timeout remaining. Instead of spiking it and saving the timeout to potentially have the ability for a run play near the goal line, Texas used that final timeout after Manning's run.

After an incomplete pass on first down, the Longhorns motioned Brown out into the flat as quickly as they could to get him into space.

"I thought our guys had great poise and composure in that final drive to execute, showed a lot of guts by Arch for sure," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian told ESPN after the game.

Manning came through on the final drive after a night of struggles. He threw three interceptions and had one of his worst games of the season as the LSU defense was consistently able to pressure him in the pocket. A pick by DJ Pickett with less than 10 minutes to go could have been the nail in the coffin for the Longhorns.

But Texas forced a three-and-out from the LSU offense and got the ball back with three minutes to go for the game-winning drive.

A disappointing first season for Lane Kiffin

Manning wasn't the only quarterback who threw three interceptions Saturday night at Tiger Stadium. LSU QB Sam Leavitt also threw three picks as the Tigers squandered numerous scoring opportunities for the second straight week.

Leavitt threw two red zone interceptions on Saturday night. Both were to Texas defensive back Jelani McDonald, who had three total interceptions in the game. The first came in the second quarter, when LSU got to the Texas 12-yard line. The second came with the Tigers leading 14-10 in the third quarter and at the Longhorns' 16-yard line.

Throw in a missed 38-yard field goal at the end of the second quarter and you can generously argue that LSU left 17 points on the table with the two picks and the missed kick. Heck, even if LSU got six points out of those three drives, it's a totally different ballgame.

Instead, the Tigers are set to drop out of the CFP rankings on Tuesday night. That's not at all what was supposed to happen when Kiffin was dramatically brought over from Ole Miss nearly a year ago.

Kiffin's hire came with immediate playoff expectations. He added players like Leavitt, offensive tackle Jordan Seaton, edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen and others through the transfer portal thanks to a healthy NIL budget.

The Tigers were a team built to win right away.

Instead, Leavitt has thrown 12 interceptions and LSU is having a hard time beating ranked opponents. You're not going to succeed in the SEC if you can't do that.

The Tigers are now 2-3 against teams ranked in the AP Top 25 in 2026. The two wins are against Texas A&M, a team that's now 4-6 and spiraling, and against Mississippi State. The Bulldogs were ranked No. 16 at the time but didn't have Kamario Taylor as he missed the game due to the toe injury that has sidelined him for the rest of the season.

Saturday night's loss is also the second straight for the Tigers at home. You have to go all the way back to 1994 — a year where LSU finished 4-7 — to find the last time the Tigers lost home games in consecutive weeks.

Sure, Texas could miss out on the College Football Playoff if it loses its last two games of the regular season. We're not going to totally rule that scenario out. Nothing is impossible.

The Longhorns' last two games are against Arkansas and Texas A&M. The Razorbacks and Aggies are a combined 3-11 in SEC play. A split will be good enough to get Texas into the playoff thanks to wins over Ohio State, Tennessee and Ole Miss along with recent wins over a pair of Tigers in Mizzou and LSU.

Manning finished 19-of-35 passing for 174 yards and ended up tied with Brown as the team's leading rusher with 35 yards. The Longhorns struggled to move the ball against the LSU defense on Saturday night and settled far too often for field goals. But it was still enough against an LSU team that was penalized 11 times for 93 yards.

This Texas team doesn't look capable of making a national title run. But it's still one of the most talented teams in the country. As long as the Longhorns are in the playoff field, they'll have a real chance.

articles.title: Everything Arch Manning Said After Leading Texas to Comeback Win vs. Lane Kiffin, LSU Amid CFP Race
articles.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning reflected on his performance after the Longhorns took down LSU by the final score of 22-21 on Saturday.
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning reflected on his performance after the Longhorns took down LSU by the final score of 22-21 on Saturday.

"In a bunch of years, I'm going to tell everyone we had a game winning drive and everyone's gonna forget the three picks," Manning told reporters after the game.

Manning threw three interceptions during the SEC clash, but connected with Raleek Brown for a game-winning touchdown in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.

LSU was effectively eliminated from the College Football Playoff with the defeat, as Manning revealed that the Longhorns discussed having "to end someone else's dream" heading into the game.

Manning, a New Orleans native, also explained how he felt winning in his home state.

"I grew up around a lot of LSU fans, so it's gonna feel good to come back for Mardi Gras or come back whenever I come home and not have them talk a bunch of crap," Manning said during his press conference (0:09 mark).

"I was pointing out to some of the teammates where I sat at these games growing up," he added. "So just coming back home, getting it done the last few seconds, it's a memory I'll have for the rest of my life."

The signal-caller detailed how Texas' flight to the game was delayed by the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop on Friday as well.

"It was actually kind of fun," Manning told reporters. "We went back to the facility, had dinner and then we had like an hour before our meeting. So we just sat in the stadium and chilled and talked, got pretty deep. It was fun."

The Longhorns took an early 7-0 lead over LSU in Saturday's contest, but the Tigers quickly tied the game at 7-7.

With Texas attempting to move back in front early in the second quarter, Manning threw an interception that allowed LSU to gain a 14-7 advantage.

The Longhorns responded with a field goal, but the Tigers still led 14-10 at halftime.

LSU pushed its lead to 21-10 with a 44-yard rushing touchdown by Dilin Jones in the third quarter, but couldn't find much success offensively afterwards.

Texas scored 12 straight points to win the game on Manning's last-second touchdown pass, while the Tigers were forced to punt on each of their final four possessions.

Head coach Steve Sarkisian's squad improved to 8-2 with the victory, remaining squarely in the CFP picture.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal se pone el 10
articles.standfirst: Valles, Jacobo Ramón, De Frutos y Roberto Fernández son los descartes, además de Grimaldo, baja por gripe
articles.summary: Valles, Jacobo Ramón, De Frutos y Roberto Fernández son los descartes, además de Grimaldo, baja por gripe
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente ya ha comunicado a la UEFA la lista de 23 jugadores con los que España afrontará el duelo ante Inglaterra, el que decide quién es primera de grupo y quién afronta los cuartos como segunda y la vuelta en campo contrario. A pesar de haber tenido a 28 jugadores en Las Rozas, el seleccionador español tuvo que hacer solo cuatro descartes. En la noche de ayer, Alejandro Grimaldo se marchó aquejado de un proceso vírico que ha afectado a varios internacionales españoles a lo largo de la semana. Los cuatro jugadores que verán el partido desde la grada del Metropolitano serán Álvaro Valles, Jacobo Ramón, De Frutos y Roberto Fernández. Es decir, el cuarto portero llamado ante los problemas de Raya para sumarse a la concentración desde el inicio, uno de los posibles debutantes, el central del Como, y dos delanteros que tuvieron minutos en Praga: De Frutos y Roberto Fernández. Pero la noticia está en la elección de dorsales. Con Oyarzabal y Lamine Yamal de vuelta, estaba el interrogante de si el delantero del Barcelona cambiaba el 19, su marca en la selección, por el 10, vacante al estar lesionado Dani Olmo. Y así ha sido. Lamine Yamal jugará ante Inglaterra con el dorsal fetiche de la historia del fútbol, el de Pelé, Maradona, Messi, Platini, Modric, Zidane (Francia), Zico.... No es la primera vez que Lamine Yamal elige el 10. Lo hizo en octubre de 2024. Entonces, en una España plagada de bajas, entre ellas la de Dani Olmo, se quedó con ese dorsal para jugar ante Dinamarca en Murcia: 1-0, gol de Zubimendi. Tres días después, ante Serbia en Córdoba (3-0), fue baja a causa de problemas musculares y el 10 fue para Rodrigo Riquelme. El 10 en la historia va unido al nombre de Cesc. Fue su dorsal en la primera época dorada: 2008-2012. Desde que el ahora entrenador del Como desapareció de la selección, lo que sucedió con la llegada de Lopetegui en septiembre de 2016, las parejas de baile del 10 han sido muchas hasta ser propiedad de Dani Olmo. Entonces el 10 fue para Thiago, su dueño en ese ciclo y cuando estuvo con Luis Enrique. El 10 ha sido el dorsal de Asensio (Mundial de Qatar), Canales, Carlos Soler, Sergi Roberto, Pedri, Ceballos (el primero de De la Fuente), Yeremy Pino (que lo cogió como Riquelme, llamado de urgencia en septiembre de 2023), Bryan Zaragoza (también entró tras una lesión), Nico Williams, Dani Olmo (su dueño actual si está), Pepelu, Lamine Yamal, Riquelme, Jesús Rodríguez y Víctor Muñoz.

articles.title: El peligro de normalizar que España gane (casi) siempre
articles.summary: Una opinión de Pedro Morata
articles.body: Yo soy de los que han vivido una selección española que no ganaba casi nunca y que casi siempre nos daba decepciones. Y también tengo la suerte de disfrutar de esta selección que desde 2010 ganó su primer Mundial en Sudáfrica. Actualmente hemos normalizado algo que no es normal y que, además, es muy extraordinario. España gana cada vez que juega. O casi siempre, que juega. En esta última etapa de Luis de la Fuente, de casi cuatro años, los números son abrumadores. Hay un primer bloque de dos partidos oficiales: El de su debut como seleccionador, el 25 de marzo de 2023, que se ganó contra Noruega 3-0 y el siguiente se perdió contra Escocia 2-0 justo tres días después, clasificatorio para la Eurocopa 2024, que al final ganaría España. Después de esos dos partidos esta es la secuencia hasta el día de hoy: - 44 partidos oficiales jugados - 37 partidos ganados - 7 partidos empatados - 0 partidos perdidos Por tanto, España y De la Fuente suman 46 partidos oficiales como seleccionador donde sólo ha perdido un partido y, como mucho, se le puede auditar una derrota en un partido amistoso contra Colombia en marzo de 2024. Fruto de lo anterior, en esta etapa De la Fuente, España ha colocado en la vitrina: - La UEFA Nations League 22/23 (la clasificación hasta la fase final es de Luis Enrique y De la Fuente dirigió semifinal y Final porque fue nombrado en noviembre de 2022 y debutó en marzo de 2023). - Eurocopa 2024, ganando a Inglaterra en la Final. - Mundial 2026, aplastando a Argentina en la Final. Esto no es normal. Y no es bueno normalizarlo, porque llegará un día que habrá una eliminación inesperada, nos echarán de una Nations League, que entonces diremos que es un gran título, cuando hasta hace poco se le negaba importancia y empezaremos a buscarle las cinco patas al gato. Así somos. Nos conocemos. Y por eso tanta victoria consecutiva (ahora mismo son 12), tantos partidos ganados(37), tantos partidos sin perder (44) , tantos títulos gordos ganados en tan poco tiempo, nos va a hacer perder la perspectiva cuando fallemos o mejor dicho cuando fallen, porque cuando pierdan serán ellos y cuando ganan somos nosotros. Así somos también. Ahora disfrutamos de un periodo en el que la gente, en la inmensa mayoría del país, se pone la camiseta de España incluso para salir de fiesta. Esa roja en la piel no era moneda de uso común. Por tanto hagamos el favor cuando la Selección nos de un disgusto (como nos ha pasado toda la vida) de quererla como ahora la queremos y la usamos ahora. Aprovecho para aportar una teoría a las muchas que se leen y se escuchan sobre esta generación de futbolistas que estamos disfrutando. Muchos dirán que es casualidad, que son coincidencias del destino porque salen cosechas buenas de diferentes canteras a la vez, otros dirán que es el seleccionador etc. Yo añado una idea: la incidencia del control económico de LaLiga en los clubes de fútbol. La camisa de fuerza del famoso Fair Play que obliga a los clubes a no malgastar dinero. Hubo una época que aquí venía cualquier tuercebotas del este, el sureste o el noreste. Se pusieron de moda, yugoslavos, rumanos, colombianos… Clubes modestos acababan fichando a auténticas extravagancias. Por ejemplo: hasta hace nada y ante los problemas de Fair Play el Barça ha sacado a Cubarsí en vez de fichar a un Chigrinsky de la vida. El Barça es un claro ejemplo de que cuando el control económico te controla, te obligas a ser ingenioso y valiente con la cantera y a darle la oportunidad a chavales que caso contrario o no se la darías, o se la darías más tarde o acabarías fichando a muchos más Vitor Roques. Vaya por delante que el Barça es uno de los clubes históricamente más comprometidos con su cantera. Podría citar decenas de jugadores tipo Ognejnovic, Drenthe en el Real Madrid; Pabon, Sabin Ilie (no confundir con el bueno Adrian) en el Valencia CF… El control económico de LaLiga no está pensado para esta finalidad, pero indirectamente posibilita que muchos más jugadores de cantera asciendan al primer equipo y tengan la posibilidad de acabar siendo jugadores de la selección española.

articles.title: Misery Index: Kyle Whittingham's sad story at Michigan just got worse
articles.summary: There is something missing from the Whittingham era at Michigan but the most glaring characteristic of his 10 games in charge is a decided lack of urgency an...
articles.body:
Lore is a powerful concept in sports, and over more than two decades, it did a number on our perception of Kyle Whittingham.

He was the guy who hadn't missed a workout in 100 years. He was the guy whose teams overachieved by playing hard-nosed, physical football that was not aesthetically pleasing but often effective. He was the guy who found future NFL players in places nobody else looked and won for so long at Utah that you had to wonder what he might be capable of at one of the sport's blue-blood jobs.

Most of all, he was intense because how else could Whittingham do all that at Utah for so many years without being a bit of a maniac?

So when the opportunity came to coach at Michigan in his mid-60s, it seemed like a natural fit. What was more in the Whittingham wheelhouse than Big Ten football, gray November days in Ann Arbor and a fan base that doesn't mind if you win ugly as long as you win big?

It fit the stereotype and the lore. It hasn't fit the reality.

There is something missing from the Whittingham era at Michigan — well, there's a lot missing, to be honest, including wins — but the most glaring characteristic of his 10 games in charge is a decided lack of urgency and intensity. It's to the point where you almost have to ask whether this is even the same guy we watched pull off some amazing feats at Utah over the years.

If Whittingham is one-and-done at Michigan, which must be on the table at this point after a 31-7 loss to Oregon, it will not just be about the record. Yes, being 5-5 at this point in the season is a disappointment for a program that aspires to compete for championships. But just as problematic are a series of things he's said that suggest Whittingham doesn't quite understand what he signed up for.

The reaction to his preseason comment about not hating Ohio State was overwrought, but then he also downplayed the Michigan State rivalry game (which Michigan also lost, 15-6). Nobody would expect Whittingham to understand every single nuance of Michigan football, but when you become the head coach of a team, part of the job is understanding what the customers (i.e., the fans) care about. Having a sense of the rivalries is a pretty big one!

But every time Whittingham steps in front of a microphone, he comes across as if the Michigan job is a timeshare rental property that he doesn't intend to ever buy. He enjoys spending time at the house and wants to take care of it, but eventually he's going to go home to the place he owns. Whether it's the rivalry issue or dragging his feet on making offensive staff changes, even after several weeks of bad results, Whittingham does not convey the same urgency that most Michigan fans feel.

Where is that understated intensity that sometimes bubbled into rage? Where is the no-excuse coach who made you feel like he could bench press as much as his linebackers?

That's the guy Michigan thought it hired, but he hasn't shown up on the job. Instead, Michigan has gotten the grandfather-philosopher version of Whittingham whose general serenity is not matching the nature of the results. If anything, the team has adopted his aura of listlessness.

It's tricky to talk about age because 66 is not that old, and plenty of people in Whittingham's age group are doing some of their best work — including Indiana's Curt Cignetti, who is 65. But something has changed at this stage of Whittingham's career, and Utah saw it too. Remember, Whittingham did not take the Michigan job until Utah had already nudged him out the door, which they would not have done without feeling confident Morgan Scalley would take the program to an even higher level. Obviously, they were right. Something about Whittingham's approach is not in touch with the current era.

Now Michigan is paying the price for misreading the situation, but there's another complication to what might be a straightforward decision. The school hasn't hired an athletic director yet, meaning any coaching decision would be driven by its highly political and sometimes messy board of regents. That's a recipe for disaster.

That puts Michigan in serious limbo until an AD is named, and time is running short before the coaching carousel really starts moving. Having such a problematic situation without a clear path out makes Michigan the most miserable fan base in America for Week 11.

ACC: It's hard to find anything new to say about the sadness of Clemson football. The era of winning big under Dabo Swinney is functionally over, and has been over for a while now, because the same things keep happening without much recognition from the head coach that the program is in a multiyear nosedive. But now, after a 20-6 loss at home to Georgia Tech — the same Georgia Tech that was 2-7 coming into the game and fired four assistant coaches last week — we might have finally reached a nadir the university can no longer abide. If you think Clemson can't tell the greatest coach in school history, a future Hall of Famer and a two-time national champion, that his services are no longer needed, a two-touchdown home loss to the ACC's last place team might have a way of forcing some honest conversations. Yes, Clemson had injuries, including to quarterback Tait Reynolds early in the game. But giving up 269 rushing yards to Georgia Tech is an indictment of the entire operation and demands accountability. Swinney's $57 million buyout (without a mitigation clause if he takes another job) is ridiculous and perhaps prohibitive. A forced separation would be painful and ugly. But so is a 2-9 record in Swinney's last 11 home games against power conference opponents.

Big 12: If you're in the administration at Florida State and talking yourself into Jimbo Fisher as the new/old head coach, it might be useful to look at a recent example of a school reaching into its past. At West Virginia, the second go-round with Rich Rodriguez simply isn't working. If anything, it's worse than ever after a 37-14 loss at home to Kansas. This is what happens when boosters who don't know anything about football beyond their nostalgia clamor for a coach who makes them feel the warm fuzzies they remember from the good old days. Rich Rod wasn't just a good coach at West Virginia from 2001-07, he was a great one — losing just five games in his final three seasons and finishing No. 5, No. 10 and No. 11 in the final AP polls. That was enough to get offered both the Alabama job and the Michigan job during that stretch, the latter of which he accepted. But trying to recreate a moment in time like that so many years later is usually a recipe for disaster. There's a reason why rock bands go from playing big stadiums at the height of their popularity to off-brand casinos at the end. The world constantly changes and moves on, and West Virginia isn't the same job it was 20 years ago in a league, the Big East, that no longer exists in football. This loss to Kansas feels like the moment when everyone realizes the past isn't coming back. At 5-5, the Mountaineers really, really needed this game to get bowl eligible with Houston and Utah to finish the season. Instead, they laid a complete egg — and it wasn't just about their awful defense, which has given up an average of 495 yards per game. The offense wasn't so hot either this time, accounting for just 262 yards. That's an all-around disgraceful effort in a very winnable matchup, and it may be time for West Virginia to think hard about where Rich Rod, The Sequel, goes from here.

SEC: It's official now that LSU's season is a $100 million bust. Does that mean it was a mistake to move heaven and earth to get Lane Kiffin to Baton Rouge, only for him to deliver this four-loss dud in Year 1? Not necessarily. Kiffin's stock has taken a beating this year, no doubt, but you can make a pretty good case that in his rush to ingratiate himself into the LSU machine, he accepted things that may not have been the best fit. Like keeping defensive coordinator Blake Baker. Or getting a quarterback with Sam Leavitt's particular skill set out of the transfer portal. Let's face it, we know a Lane Kiffin team when we see one — and this ain't it. This is not how Kiffin wants to play football, but he's working his way through it. That should end now. Lane needs to get back to being Lane — social media and all — and that will hopefully begin after the heartbreak of a last-second, 22-21 loss to Texas. After whiffing on both monster opportunities at home against Alabama and Texas, LSU is out of the playoff mix. Given the drama they caused with their bevy of local judges and bloviating politicians, there are celebrations around the SEC. Hopefully this unleashes Kiffin, because what is the point of going from Ole Miss to LSU if he's too intimidated by the place to be himself?

Group of Six: New Mexico's fan base understands more than anyone how fleeting moments of success can be. Particularly in this era, fan bases understand that successful coaches will get lured away to the power conferences and continuing to win will depend on a game of coaching roulette. So nobody at New Mexico is going to be mad when Jason Eck gets the kind of job offer he can't turn down, most likely at the end of this month. What they'll be mad about, or at least a little sad about, is that they didn't fully maximize this run with a CFP appearance. That's off the table now for New Mexico after a pretty shocking 21-17 loss to UNLV. Though the Rebels were the preseason favorites to win the Mountain West, they fumbled their way to double-digit underdog status by the time this game kicked off. Now, the Lobos are almost in must-win territory next week at Wyoming if they want to win the conference title.

Luke Fickell: Just when you thought you were off the hot seat, some really bad football pulls you right back in. On Oct. 24, Wisconsin was 5-2 after a big home win over Southern Cal. It looked like the administration's decision to give Fickell another year and more resources to build his roster was paying off. Some were even whispering about the Badgers being a sneaky playoff contender. Then, on Halloween, they went to Iowa and got thumped. No big deal, right? Iowa is really good. But now, after a 24-21 loss to Maryland (against a backup quarterback no less), the entire picture looks different. At 6-4, with some very winnable games left against Purdue and Minnesota, Wisconsin's improvement this season is undeniable. But you can't lose to a previously 3-6 Maryland team that fired Mike Locksley weeks ago and not expect a lot of heat. Coming off two losing seasons, can Wisconsin really make a coaching change if Fickell goes 8-4 in his prove-it year? Probably not. But if it's 6-6 or even 7-5, who knows. Losing to Maryland could make all the difference in a multimillion dollar decision.

Lincoln Riley: After Jayden Maiava threw a crushing interception near the gold line with about 6 ½ minutes remaining at Indiana, CBS cameras panned over to Riley, who was sort of bent over in frustration on the sideline. It was understandable. Down 20-13, that play was USC's shot to tie a game they'd basically played on even terms. In some ways, it was USC's last, best shot at getting into the playoff picture. Instead, like most of USC's other big, defining moments during Riley's five seasons, it was a reminder that the Trojans have not come far enough to do what he was hired to do. The painful part for Riley is that both this game and the loss to Oregon back in September were there for the taking. Had USC won either of them, they'd have had enough margin for error to lay an egg at Wisconsin and not get penalized too harshly. Whether it was that mistake by Maiava or the missed 27-yard field goal at the start of the fourth quarter, that entire 60 minutes illustrated why Indiana is so good at winning close games and USC is not. There is just a certain, difficult-to-define toughness and resolve that gets Indiana through those moments time and again. And at USC, there's an equally difficult-to-define Murphy's Law vibe where the exact wrong thing will happen predictably. With UCLA now 10-0 and closer to CFP-bound, we could be setting up for a last stand at the Rose Bowl where Riley can either win back hearts and minds by playing spoiler or perhaps offer a final verdict on his disappointing tenure.

Greg Schiano: The whole point of Rutgers pushing its way into the Big Ten was to eventually make enough money through its conference membership that it wouldn't have to settle for bad football. And yet here we are, a dozen years into being a Big Ten program, and Rutgers can't afford the $28 million it would take to get rid of a coaching staff that is 2-8 this year after a 31-0 loss at home to Nebraska. That was the essence of athletic director Keli Zinn's announcement earlier in the week that Schiano would return. Even though expectations have not been met and standards have not been lowered, Rutgers is giving one more year to a coach who is 16-45 in the Big Ten. What does that mean in tangible terms? Barring a course correction that is, frankly, hard to envision, we're going to do this all over again next year. Rutgers fans will spend an entire offseason mad at the administration. The atmosphere around the program will be toxic. And much like Florida State this year with Mike Norvell, the season will be a long march of paper bags over heads, booing at lineup introductions and airplanes with messages flying overhead. Nobody ever wants to spend $28 million on a fired coaching staff, but if all that comes to pass, it'll seem like a bargain.

James Franklin: We may need Pablo Torre to investigate what the heck happened during Virginia Tech's bye week. After winning at Clemson on Oct. 24, the Hokies were 6-2 and in good position to have the kind of Year 1 under Franklin that would really push the program forward and immediately justify the big financial investments it took to get him in Blacksburg. Then came the bye week, and all Virginia Tech has done since then is stink up the ACC. Last weekend, the Hokies fell behind SMU 44-14 before making the score look a little better in a 51-28 loss. This week, the same thing happened at home against Stanford. After starting the game with three defensive stops, Virginia Tech gave up three touchdowns in a row and fell hopelessly behind before finally losing 40-22. Make no mistake, Virginia Tech was mediocre before the bye week too. But this collapse is going to deflate a fan base that had been all-in on the Franklin plan since he became available last October.

A&M's offense hit a new low: It has been ugly in Aggieland all season, but when you put this offense on the field against a great defense like Tennessee's, it turns into a tragicomedy. In a 22-7 loss at home, Texas A&M managed just 179 yards of offense, one-third of which came on a 61-yard touchdown drive in the second quarter. Their other 11 drives averaged 11.7 yards with two turnovers. Quarterback Marcel Reed, who has had a truly awful and confounding season (he was pretty good last year!), completed 9-of-22 for 71 yards. Head coach Mike Elko snapped at a reporter this week for asking about his confidence in offensive coordinator Holmon Wiggins, calling it a "stupid question," but it's actually the only question that matters right now for the Aggies. At 4-6, with a road game at Oklahoma and a home game against Texas remaining, Elko is looking 4-8 square in the face just a year after making the CFP and signing a big contract extension. If the offense isn't significantly better next season, Elko will find himself on a smoldering hot seat. He knows it, too, calling the offense "inept" and "completely non-functional" after the game while emphasizing that "It's my fault. I own it."

Tosh isn't getting the message: There's been an interesting dynamic this season at Cal where first-year coach Tosh Lupoi continues to show that he's learning on the job (to put it kindly) and general manager Ron Rivera delivers strange but very candid on-the-record criticisms of the work he's doing. "He has bumped his head a lot," Rivera said on KNBR radio recently. "I mean, we've talked a lot, tried to give him a lot of advice, point him in the right direction. Some of it he's been very receptive to and other portions he hasn't." It's fair to wonder what Rivera thought as he watched Lupoi, down 9-0 at Virginia late in the first half, send out his team in a bizarre formation on fourth-and-goal and snap it to tight end Mason Mini, who subsequently threw an interception. Though it was just one of many bad moments in a 36-7 loss, Cal is now 3-7 and has to be wondering if it made a mistake. Lupoi has a lot of experience as a defensive coach and recruiter, but Rivera is basically comfortable admitting in public that Cal has a coaching problem. You have to give a first-year head coach room to grow and make mistakes, but you can't tolerate incompetence. We'll see soon where Cal thinks its program is on that delicate spectrum.

articles.summary: El ex del Tottenham brilla con el Inter: suma tres asistencias en tres partidos como titular
articles.body: Diop Tehuti Djed-Hotep Spence (Kensington, 2000) es uno de los personajes más peculiares del 'planeta fútbol'. Sus pintorescos 'outfits', sus carismáticas rastas, sus llamativas gafas de sol, y los guiños a 'Spider-man' en su presentación con el Inter han dado lugar a lo que algunos ya han bautizado como 'Spenceverso'. Una nueva realidad en la que el ex del Tottenham, fichado este verano a cambio de 30 millones de euros, comienza a llenar el vacío dejado por Denzel Dumfries en el lateral derecho. Le ha costado, eso sí: las molestias físicas que arrastraba tras brillar como lateral izquierdo en el Mundial con Inglaterra le impidieron estrenarse como titular en el 'calcio' hasta el 31 de octubre. Se estrenó, para colmo, con derrota en el 'Derby della Madonnina' contra el Milan (3-1). Dejó, eso sí, buenas sensaciones. "Un par de apariciones como suplente contra Parma y Brujas, una hora frente al Shakhtar, y luego tres titularidades: en la derrota ante el Milan —en la que jugó admirablemente—, frente al Feyenoord y contra el Como. Tres partidos difíciles y cruciales para el Inter, donde Chivu ha elegido a Spence de forma constante. Y no es casualidad", refleja 'La Gazzetta dello Sport'. En el triunfo en Champions ante el Feyenoord (0-3), en su segundo partido jugando desde el inicio, destapó el 'tarro de las esencias': asistió a Yann Bisseck en el 0-1 y sirvió en bandeja el 0-2 a Pio Esposito. No es de extrañar que resultara elegido 'MVP'. "Dominó el partido en los primeros 35 minutos, enviando dos pases magistrales desde la banda derecha que permitieron al Inter adelantarse rápidamente en el marcador. Además, mantuvo una gran precisión en sus pases, desplegando una velocidad vertiginosa y demostrando su gran potencial dentro del esquema 1-3-5-2 de Cristian Chivu. A nivel táctico, con su velocidad punta, permite que el equipo esté significativamente menos expuesto a los contraataques del rival", se justificaba el 'Panel de Analistas Técnicos' de la UEFA. "Agradezco la victoria y los tres puntos. Estoy contento con mi rendimiento. Me estoy adaptando bien; el equipo y el entrenador me han recibido con los brazos abiertos. Me están ayudando mucho", admitía Spence, que volvió a reivindicarse en el triunfo ante el Como (2-0): sirvió el 'pase de la muerte' para que, nuevamente, Pio Esposito 'abriera la lata' en el 12'. Por fin, tras pasar por Fulham, Middlesbrough, Nottingham Forest, Rennes, Genoa, Leeds y Tottenham, parece haber encontrado su sitio en San Siro. "El motor de Djed Spence pasó de cero a cien en un abrir y cerrar de ojos. El inglés se ha impuesto con arrogancia en el flanco derecho del Inter, obligando a Chivu, al menos recientemente, a interrumpir el trabajo que había comenzado meses atrás para convertir a Diouf en la alternativa de lateral derecho que le faltó durante mucho tiempo la temporada pasada y que había buscado durante todo el mercado de fichajes, hasta la llegada del exjugador del Tottenham", apostilla 'Corriere dello Sport'. Chivu, por su parte, está encantado con el 'Spenceverso' que se abre ante sus ojos: "Cuando lo elegimos sabíamos lo que podía aportarnos. Desafortunadamente, durante dos meses no contamos con él, e intentamos que recuperara el ritmo haciéndolo jugar. En los últimos partidos ha jugado bien, pero aún puede mejorar mucho". Nadie, eso sí, ha sido tan elocuente al referirse al lateral inglés como el díscolo Paolo di Canio: "Puede jugar con los ojos vendados en Italia. Es un jugador que fue titular en el Mundial con la tercera mejor selección del mundo. No estamos hablando de un cualquiera”. “Tiene una zurda increíble y una técnica excepcional. Ante el Como dio una asistencia digna de la Premier League. Un pase potente; o se marcan en propia puerta o marca tu compañero. También tiene la habilidad técnica para sacar el balón desde atrás. A veces se desconecta, es cierto, pero si corrige ese defecto, le resultará mucho más fácil jugar como lateral, dada su condición física, calidad y técnica”, insistía el ex de Lazio, Juventus, Nápoles, Milan y West Ham, entre otros, a 'FcInter1908'. El 'calcio' ha entrado en un nuevo 'universo'.

articles.title: Baena juega en casa
articles.standfirst: El andaluz será anfitrión de España ante Inglaterra en el partido del Metropolitano.
articles.summary: El andaluz será anfitrión de España ante Inglaterra en el partido del Metropolitano.
articles.body: España será local frente a Inglaterra en un partido en el que tres de los convocado por Luis de la Fuente juegan en casa. Baena, Barrios y Pubill serán anfitriones de España en un partido en el que el Metropolitano se llenará para enfrentar a la número uno y la número cuatro del ranking FIFA. "Va a ser un partido muy especial porque sé cómo es la gente del Atleti, la gente de Madrid. Van a apretar muchísimo, como en cada partido que se juega en el Metropolitano. Esperemos que sea así porque los vamos a necesitar", aseguraba Baena. De los tres colchoneros del grupo, es precisamente el de Roquetas de Mar el que vive su momento más dulce. No sólo con su club, sino también con la selección. En junio fue al Mundial después de firmar una temporada discreta en el Atlético. Le costó adaptarse y se quedó lejos de la versión que venía mostrando en el Villarreal. Sólo dos goles y tres asistencias en una temporada en la que sufrió dos lesiones musculares y apendicitis no era un saldo suficiente para un jugador como él, pero eso no le impidió estar entre los elegidos por De la Fuente para afrontar el reto de la segunda estrella. Y ahí apareció el mejor Álex. No jugó en el debut ante Cabo Verde, pero fue titular en el resto de partidos. Marcó el gol de la victoria ante Uruguay, asistió contra Austria y fue determinante en el juego de la selección en el camino hacia el campeonato del mundo. Su golpeo de balón, su calidad y su compromiso defensivo lo convirtieron en indiscutible para Luis de la Fuente y uno de los mejores jugadores del campeonato. "Hay jugadores que tienen un gen especial y carácter de selección. Álex ha rendido muy bien siempre que ha estado conmigo", confesaba el técnico riojano. Probablemente ese "carácter selección" es el que este verano llevó a Baena a entrar en la historia del fútbol español, ya que se convirtió en el primer futbolista en ser campeón de Europa (2024), campeón olímpico (2024) y campeón del mundo (2026). Y además, lo logró de forma consecutiva. "Es un gran logro para mi carrera", confiesa. Esta temporada, su rendimiento en el Atlético de Madrid está siendo sobresaliente. A estas alturas ya mejora con creces sus estadísticas del año pasado y acumula cinco goles y cuatro asistencias en los poco más de 1000 minutos que acumula dentro de los 16 partidos en los que ha participado. Simeone está encantado con él. "Baena está muy bien. El año pasado empezó muy bien, pero las lesiones no le dejaron estar en su mejor versión y terminó haciendo una temporada de la que seguramente él esperaba más. El Mundial lo llevó a un lugar diferente. Está muchísimo más seguro de sí mismo y tiene unas condiciones fantásticas. Está más contundente, más fuerte y más seguro. Es el jugador que fuimos a buscar", confesaba el argentino.

articles.title: "Guardiaciviles con las espadas desenvainadas..."
articles.standfirst: Historias de la primera derrota de Inglaterra lejos de las Islas, en 1929 en el Metropolitano
articles.summary: Historias de la primera derrota de Inglaterra lejos de las Islas, en 1929 en el Metropolitano
articles.body: Inglaterra vuelve a poner el Metropolitano en su mapa. Es la segunda vez que lo hace. La primera fue en el viejo estadio, el de Reina Victoria, y es una fea herida de guerra en la historia de la selección inglesa. Una de esas que, por más que pasen los años, no desaparece. Y va camino de cumplir un siglo. Porque aquello ocurrió el 15 de mayo de 1929. Ese día, España se convirtió en la primera selección no británica en derrotar a los profesionales ingleses. Los amateurs ingleses habían caído en Copenhague (2-1, en mayo de 1910), pero a los pros solo les habían derrotado escoceses, galeses e irlandeses. Ese fue un triunfo que se contó con entusiasmo en España. Nunca se había vivido tanta expectación antes de un partido de la selección. Entonces, lo normal era cerrar dos partidos, uno en cada país. Los ingleses no creían que mereciera la pena invitar a Londres a rivales que no estaban a su altura. En su excursión continental, Inglaterra se había paseado por París (1-4) y Bruselas (1-5). En los días previos al partido de Madrid, la prensa inglesa daba por sentado que sus jugadores darían una muestra más de que su fútbol era inalcanzable al otro lado del Canal de la Mancha. El partido fue presentado en la prensa inglesa como el cierre del viaje de su selección. Era la primera vez que uno de sus equipos nacionales se adentraba en suelo ibérico. Destacaban la enorme expectación que el encuentro había despertado entre los aficionados españoles y las dificultades para encontrar entradas. Lo que se vivió aquel miércoles 15 de mayo en Madrid causó asombro entre los periodistas ingleses. “Esperar una cola de más de una milla y durante horas para ver a tu equipo nacional contra otro país es algo que no tiene precedentes en el fútbol británico. Pero esa fue la experiencia de muchos de los 30.000 espectadores que acudieron al Metropolitano cargados de un entusiasmo fuera de lugar”, se lee en la crónica de The Times. Porque nadie en Inglaterra esperaba lo que iba a suceder. Menos aún cuando, a los 20 minutos, los ingleses ya habían marcado dos veces. Otra goleada, como las de París y Bruselas, parecía estar cocinándose. Sin embargo... De repente, en un estadio en el que no se sabe cuánta gente había por encima de lo legal, el Metropolitano se convirtió en un manicomio. Antes del descanso, España empató. Gaspar Rubio marcó en el minuto 40 y Jaime Lazcano, dos más tarde. La derrota de España ya no parecía segura. Los ingleses estaban aturdidos. Por la reacción de España, por el clima del estadio y por el calor. En el descanso tuvieron que ponerse toallas y trapos empapados para rebajar los efectos del calor madrileño en el día de su patrón, San Isidro. A falta de un cuarto de hora, Inglaterra volvió a tomar el mando. El belga John Langenus, considerado el mejor árbitro del mundo, castigó una caída de Adcock como penalti. Carter, que había marcado el 0-1, puso el 2-3. Volvía la normalidad. Pero España estaba embravecida. Con los ingleses agotados, al calor se sumaba que llevaban semanas fuera de casa y de tren en tren, a falta de diez minutos empató Gaspar Rubio. Y entonces ocurrió algo que dejó boquiabiertos a los ingleses. Así lo contó The Times: “El partido estaba en un momento cargado de emoción. Cuando España empató (3-3), una muchedumbre superó las barandillas y corrió hacia el goleador para abrazarlo. Detrás de ellos apareció una compañía de la Guardia Civil con las espadas desenvainadas para disolver a la multitud. Les costó lograrlo. Y después de algunos minutos se pudo reanudar el partido”. Y quedaba la traca final. El gol de Goiburu a falta de ocho minutos. La histeria fue total. Al acabar el partido, los guardias civiles tuvieron que intervenir de nuevo para que los jugadores pudieran alcanzar los vestuarios. Era una victoria de España para la historia. Aunque la prensa de la época era poco amiga de regalar flores. “Justa la victoria española, a pesar de haber jugado tan mal, bastante mal. Los ingleses constituyen un buen equipo, un conjunto notable, pero no lo excepcional que se suponía”, se leía en La Libertad de Madrid, en un artículo en el que se mezclaban elogios y zarandeos. En la prensa inglesa se pasó de puntillas sobre el asunto. Las breves crónicas resaltaban el cansancio de sus jugadores. Pero la derrota en Madrid hizo daño. La FA invitó a España para jugar en Londres en diciembre de 1931. Era algo que los ingleses solo habían hecho antes dos veces con selecciones continentales. Las dos con Bélgica: 6-1 en 1923 y 4-0 un año después. Los ingleses prepararon con mimo aquel partido. Lo ganaron por 7-1, en Highbury. Pero la herida del Metropolitano nunca cerraría.

articles.title: Latif Issman, así es el "animal" que estudia Comercio Internacional y ya ha firmado por el Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Radiografía del centrocampista ghanés que llegó a la UD Logroñés en su último año de juvenil, convenció a Mendía en un entrenamiento y se hizo indiscutible en Primera Federación antes de cerrar su fichaje con los blancos: arrancará en verano con el Castilla
articles.summary: Radiografía del centrocampista, nacido en Ghana y con pasaporte español, que llegó a la UD Logroñés en su último año de juvenil, convenció a Unai Mendía en un entrenamiento y se hizo indiscutible en Primera Federación antes de cerrar su llegada al club blanco este jueves
articles.body: Latif Issman y Manex Rezola compartían coche para ir a entrenarse con el primer equipo de la UD Logroñés. Habían coincidido en el juvenil de División de Honor y los dos empezaban a abrirse paso entre los mayores. Manex se marchó primero al Real Madrid y actualmente está a caballo entre el Real Madrid C y el Castilla. Latif hará el mismo viaje el próximo verano, cuando se incorpore directamente al Castilla. Como adelantó MARCA y confirmó después Fabrizio Romano con su ya famoso here we go, Issman ya ha firmado (lo hizo el pasado jueves) y es el primer gran refuerzo del club blanco para su filial. No se descarta que participe en la pretemporada del primer equipo. La operación se ha cerrado por encima de los 200.000 euros de su cláusula de rescisión y vuelve a reflejar la buena sintonía entre ambos clubes tras el precedente de Manex. Latif acaba de cumplir 20 años. Nació en Ghana el 1 de noviembre de 2006, tiene pasaporte español, estudia Comercio Internacional y procede de una familia trabajadora. Su trayectoria futbolística se ha gestado íntegramente en Logroño. Empezó en la SD Logroñés y pasó a la UD Logroñés en su último año de juvenil, cuando se estrenó en División de Honor. Le bastó un curso para llamar la atención del primer equipo y un solo entrenamiento para cambiar el plan que el club tenía para él. Hay un número que Latif suele escribir cuando quiere hacer un guiño a los suyos. El 26004 es el código postal de su barrio en Logroño. Allí están sus amigos de toda la vida, con los que sigue quedando desde que se hizo un sitio en el primer equipo. Abierto y muy apegado a su gente, compagina el fútbol con unos estudios que le interesan de verdad. La idea inicial de la secretaría técnica era que recalase en el filial al concluir su etapa formativa. Sin embargo, Unai Mendía le llamó para completar una sesión con los mayores y, tras comprobar su despliegue, decidió quedárselo en el primer equipo. Con 1,82 metros de estatura y una condición física imponente, el centrocampista diestro no tardó en hacerse sitio. Tuvo minutos en la fase de ascenso y, ya en Primera Federación, se consolidó como el motor del equipo. Superó los 660 minutos en el tramo inicial del campeonato pese a perderse algún partido por sanción. Mendía le bautizó como "el animal" por cómo compite. Quique García, exdirector deportivo del club, vio en él un "perfil Premier". Ya en pretemporada, en un amistoso frente al Real Zaragoza, dejó muestras de lo que puede aportar como centrocampista de ida y vuelta. Presiona arriba, tiene piernas para recuperar metros cuando el rival supera la primera línea y sostiene al equipo en defensa. Representado por la agencia MS Sports, Issman puede jugar como pivote defensivo o como interior. Destaca por su despliegue, su valentía en los duelos divididos y su juego directo. Su gran carta de presentación es la conducción. En cuanto recupera la pelota, es capaz de romper la primera línea de presión rival con potencia, generar superioridades o abrir espacios para sus compañeros. En Valdebebas tendrá el reto de mejorar la toma de decisiones en los últimos metros, especialmente a la hora de soltar el balón tras una arrancada. El Madrid venía siguiéndole desde el pasado mercado de verano, cuando ya estuvo cerca de ficharlo, y aceleró los contactos en otoño (ESPN informó de ellos el pasado 30 de octubre) para adelantarse a otros pretendientes. Latif terminará el curso en Las Gaunas con un objetivo claro. Antes de hacer las maletas rumbo a Valdebebas y reencontrarse con Manex, quiere devolver a la UD Logroñés al fútbol profesional. La relación entre el Real Madrid y la UD Logroñés ya funciona por ambas partes, en los dos sentidos. Hace una década, el vínculo entre Emilio Butragueño y Juan José Guerreros facilitó que Sergio Reguilón jugara dos veces cedido en Las Gaunas, entre 2015 y 2017, y que Alejandro Sotillos llegara en 2017. Ya hubo un precedente en la otra dirección cuando el Madrid se llevó a Jordan Gaspar en 2016. Desde entonces, la UD Logroñés ha creado su primer equipo cadete, reforzado su cuerpo técnico y construido una ciudad deportiva con residencia. El Juvenil A ascendió a División de Honor en 2019, se ha mantenido en la máxima categoría y llegó a disputar la Copa del Rey juvenil. De ese equipo salieron Manex Rezola, procedente del Baskonia, y Latif. Ambos dieron el salto al primer equipo con Mendia y acabaron fichando por el Madrid. El club blanco se llevó a Manex y ha cerrado para el verano de 2027 la incorporación al Castilla de Issman. El viaje entre ciudades que ya no va sólo en una dirección.

articles.title: Why are England's biggest stars playing abroad?
articles.summary: Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon are three of England's current biggest stars, but all have chosen to play their club football abroad.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich's Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham, Barcelona's Anthony Gordon - three of England's star players, all of whom are playing their club football abroad.

The Premier League is widely regarded as the most competitive league in the world with the greatest financial muscle, but that does not always translate to the biggest individual profiles and, increasingly, star names are looking elsewhere.

Since Cristiano Ronaldo won the Ballon d'Or in 2008, for example, only Rodri in 2024 was playing in England at the time of being crowned the best player in the world. Michael Owen, in 2001, was the last Englishman to do so while in England.

The trend of English players going abroad has gathered pace since a teenage Jadon Sancho signed for Borussia Dortmund in 2017 and that is reflected in this current Three Lions squad - seven of the initial 25 play outside England.

"Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane were decisive for us in the World Cup and I see no reason they won't be in the future," said England boss Thomas Tuchel when talking about his big stars playing outside of their home country.

"It's good that Anthony has stepped up now. He is the third one. There is obviously a relevance to them playing abroad but I don't see that a player who plays in the Premier League cannot step up and be decisive for us."

At the World Cup in the summer and during the last international break, however, it was those three players' goals and assists that proved decisive.

Currently there are 43 English players on the Football Association's radar playing their club football in Europe.

The FA's technical director John McDermott believes it is a "huge positive" to have so many players playing across Europe.

"I spoke to a couple of the boys that are playing abroad at the moment," he told BBC Sport. "The exposure they get in those leagues, playing Champions League or European football, where you're not necessarily having to bang out 55 games, but you still have got time to do your weight training and your gym work.

"Often if you're playing in the English competition or in the EFL, where it's 46 games - you know it's game, game, game, which is fantastic - but for some players that opportunity to get the training in-between and to practise developing on technique or other areas, there's benefits to that."

McDermott was previously at Tottenham Hotspur and says that even when he was in club football, he was a "big believer" in players going abroad to "develop character" and "independence".

"I think being in another changing room and learning another language just puts you under the pressure to adapt," he added.

"And I think for any young person that ability not only to become technically, tactically more adept, but also culturally have to pick up something else - it's huge and prevents people from becoming complacent or just getting used to the same old, same old."

Gordon said in the recent international break he feels he gets more respect now he plays for one of Europe's elite sides, compared with when he was at Newcastle.

"I think he's always been respected," McDermott said.

"I remember when Trips (Kieran Trippier) came back, and Trips was a good player, but when he came back from Atletico (Madrid) I noticed he was just maybe tighter technically and noticed there was a change that Kieran came back with.

"So I'm not sure if he's respected more ... but I think you want all of the players - whether they stay in England [or not] - every six months you see this sort of incremental step where they've added something, another dimension to the game.

"That can sometimes come in this country, obviously, playing with different players, being in new competitions, but I think going abroad definitely helps that.

"And I've seen that with Anthony already and some of the other boys. They come back, it's four months since you've seen them and there's another dimension there."

McDermott is keen to make clear that developing in England can still be of a huge benefit and that Jarell Quansah and Jobe Bellingham, two of England's squad who are now playing in Germany, also played in the EFL.

"There's all different ways, I don't think there's this elixir, I don't think there's this magic formula, 'this is the way'," McDermott said.

England reached the semi-finals of the World Cup for just the third time in their history in the summer.

McDermott was asked if he thought now the Three Lions had more players abroad, it could help develop England's style or performance in major tournaments.

"Yeah, possibly. Again don't underestimate if you're playing now in the Champions League at an English club," he said.

"We would like more players in the pipeline. I think at the moment we're on about 26% or 27% English-qualified players playing the Premier League.

"We've got 40 to 50 players playing at Champions League quality and playing in European football, top Premier League clubs, so let's not underestimate our own product."

McDermott says it is clear the impact having players in different countries is having on the squad, but it is then down to the manager to blend the style.

"I think the different cultural experiences they get, the different exposure they get to play in different types of football is fantastic.

"But still, the England manager has got to try and find that singular blend when they come back of the English players, the Spanish players, the German players, the Italian players, it's all sort of an eclectic mix that they're bringing."

People did not respect 'quality and IQ' in England

Gordon has impressed since making his move to Barcelona in the summer with three goals and five assists in 15 appearances in all competitions.

The 25-year-old is regularly lining up with some of the best players in the world, in a front line alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha.

The lure of European giants like Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is hard for any player to turn down.

Arsenal's approach for Vinicius Jr this summer was always going to be hard to complete as the famous white shirt and lifestyle in Madrid is, for most players, the pinnacle.

But does moving abroad to one of Europe's top clubs also alter people's perceptions of English players?

"I always felt in England, people respected me because I was fast and I pressed, but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with," Gordon said in a recent interview with ITV.

"Only the players I play with ever seem to notice that. I think now I'm at Barcelona and I play a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are actually starting to take notice that I'm not just quick."

Gordon produced some standout moments in the World Cup, assisting both of Kane's goals in the last-32 win over DR Congo, winning a penalty in England's last-16 win over Mexico and scoring the goal to put England ahead in the semi-final against Argentina.

Captain Kane said the winger is "showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England" and that Gordon is "relishing" being one of England's "main men".

"I think it's great," added England and Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin. "The fact that we've got top-level English players playing abroad now at top European clubs, I think it's only good for English football and us as a national team.

"You see they bring different experiences that they're learning from overseas and they bring it into this group and I think as you can see they're only growing in confidence and as players and I think it's only a positive thing."
