articles.title: Women's Super League: How Aston Villa Women are reclaiming identity
articles.summary: Aston Villa Women are celebrating an important 30-year milestone on Sunday - but how are they trying to reclaim their identity?
articles.body:
A club's true identity always shows in a local derby and Aston Villa hope to impose theirs when they face rivals Birmingham City on Sunday.

Villa have not had a smooth ride of it this season after a winless start led to the sacking of former manager Natalia Arroyo at the end of September.

The Spaniard helped stabilise Villa during her two years in charge but they lacked consistency, and it left some wondering what their identity really was.

Brian Sorensen is the man in charge of changing that on the pitch now, while there are others off it who are transforming Villa behind the scenes.

"Aston Villa is a club of heart. We put a lot into everything we do," managing director Maggie Murphy told BBC Sport.

"I think a lot of people know we try to do everything the right way, the proper way. We're a club that is the heart of 'proper football' in many ways."

So what are Villa doing this season to get in touch with their values?

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Sunday's Women's Super League match with Birmingham (14:00 GMT) marks 30 years since the team officially took the Aston Villa name.

Sorensen hoes it will be the perfect opportunity to showcase who Villa are on the pitch.

"There's a lot of history in this club which maybe not many people know. We need to showcase that," said interim manager Sorensen.

"We want to be really hard-working and humble - like the area we are from - and have a clear identity of how we attack and defend.

"It's trying to align all of that, making sure that we are a team that is recognised, that is one the other teams will fear playing against."

They will celebrate this crucial point in their history in the second city derby at Villa Park, and inform fans of a research project they are undertaking this season.

The project is called 'Roots, Rise and Reach' and hopes to uncover periods of the women's team's history that have never been documented before.

They have already found a newspaper report from 1957 detailing a game between an unofficial Aston Villa Ladies team and Birmingham City.

"It's huge piece of work that we're doing just to understand our own heritage and where we've come from," said Murphy.

"We're very aware that our roots go much further [than 1996]. We're going back decades at the moment trying to uncover some of that history.

"I think it's really important to know where we've come from, because that gives us a sense of identity that maybe we don't always have."

Diving into the club's history is one way Villa are hoping to engage fans this season.

They are trying to grow attendances as part of the club's five-year strategy and last season set up fan forums for the first time.

In response to feedback, they have changed age categories on their ticketing, introduced hospitality season tickets and hosted podcasts with former players and comedians to improve matchday experiences.

They have also been advertising upcoming games on 'digi-vans' throughout the country in the hope of attracting neutral women's football fans.

"There are plenty of floating fans in women's football so we are trying to grab as many as we can and make sure they have the best possible day," added Murphy.

"They might not support Villa the first time they come, but they might after three, four games and buy themselves a claret and blue scarf.

"That's our drive. We want to build this club sustainably and generate the funds that can then go into the football side of the business."

All of these efforts are part of a wider club ambition to be sustainable and ultimately deliver success on the pitch.

Murphy's task is to make the women's team financially stable, drive revenue and improve atmosphere at games.

She works in tandem with Marisa Ewers, director of women's football, who oversees recruitment, contract renewals and football staff management.

"We want it to be super coherent across both sides. In a really crude way, my job is to make money and Marissa's job is to spend it," said Murphy.

"Our teams work really closely together. Last year, we only had two people in the club that were 100% dedicated to the women's business side. Today, we have nine.

"We are investing in revenue-generating areas. I definitely want us to be competing at the highest possible level consistently, but with heart.

"We want to feel like we have contributed to the story of women's football in this country."

Villa's season is starting to look up. They currently sit ninth with two wins and four draws from their opening nine matches.

They drew with Arsenal at the start of this month after beating Birmingham City in a penalty shootout in their Women's League Cup tie.

With successive matches against newly promoted sides Birmingham and Charlton coming up, can Villa take a step closer to where they want to be?

"Where we are today is born of the hard work of lots of people that have come before us. We need to recognise that and start to steady the ship," said Murphy.

"Villa has not been in the WSL for that long. People forget that. We're still in a very transitional phase - as is the wider women's football ecosystem."

articles.title: Spain v England: How Unai Simon became world's best goalkeeper
articles.summary: As Spain prepare to host England in the Nations League, BBC Sport columnist Guillem Balague charts the rise of Unai Simon to become the world's best keeper.
articles.body:
Peter Schmeichel handed Unai Simon the Yashin Trophy and the room applauded warmly. Then the world's best goalkeeper spent his time talking about everybody else.

Simon thanked his parents and his brother. He thanked his girlfriend for being an "oasis of tranquillity", and the friends from home who remind him that "many of us in this room are privileged".

'La cuadrilla', the gang of lifelong friends that is a traditional part of Basque culture, has a WhatsApp group of its own, and he takes them on holiday every summer.

He thanked his coaches and team-mates. Like Simon, none of them are regulars on the covers of the media.

Then he talked about a man who could not be in the room at last month's Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, but whose influence lives on - Simon's youth academy mentor Koldo Asua, who died in 2021.

The Spain and Athletic Club number one is not your archetypal superstar. In fact, he is the complete opposite.

He stays away from the headlines and is relatively low profile when compared with some of the game's other goalkeepers. His position as Spain's number is regularly questioned - as was the decision to name him as the world's best.

In the part-beauty pageant election that is the Ballon d'Or, being low key can work against you, but the case on the pitch is easy to state - even though it rattles those who see the Premier League as the highest standard reachable.

Was Raya robbed & how did Europe react to Kane's Ballon d'Or win?

Back to the award. Most acceptance speeches are lists of names. This one drew a portrait of a man, and it explains why the voters got it right.

Simon's mentor Asua spent 13 years in Bilbao working with young Athletic Club players, helping them keep their family ties and their studies alive next to football.

Simon told the Palladium Asua changed how he understood the game, and that what matters is "the legacy one leaves when this is over" - being remembered as a good person and a good team-mate.

He then turned to ex-Spain and Athletic goalkeeper Jose Angel Iribar, 83 years old and still an ambassador for the club.

Iribar, who holds the all-time appearances record at Athletic with 614 matches, wore black as a homage to legendary goalkeeper Levin Yashin - the Russian 'Black Spider' - and Simon wears the same colour as a tribute to Iribar.

Simon's parents also got a mention, because they raised him with values later reinforced at Athletic: respect for authority, a work ethic and keeping close to people who love you.

Before Spain's World Cup final triumph, Simon spoke about the natural order in which other goalkeepers could soon replace him. Arsenal's David Raya is one of those players in that queue.

Before England's Nations League visit to Spain on Sunday, Simon keeps his place with that competition beside him. Raya and Joan Garcia must wait for their moment to take the number one shirt of the best national team in the world.

Spain won the World Cup and Simon conceded the fewest goals during the tournament, which earned him the Golden Glove.

He conceded a single goal in the whole competition and kept seven clean sheets. His longest run without conceding lasted about 650 minutes, beating the 517-minute record of Italy's Walter Zenga at the 1990 tournament.

After the tournament, Simon talked about not having had much to do.

"If my gloves could talk, they would say they have not worked as hard as other goalkeepers' gloves," he said. As if it had all been that easy.

The team trusts him so much they know he will be there when needed, and his involvement in build-up is part of how Spain play.

Behind that summer sits a longer body of work: the Nations League, the European Championship and, in 2023-24, the Zamora Trophy - given to the keeper with the lowest goals conceded to games ratio in Spain - the first for an Athletic goalkeeper since Iribar in 1970.

He has not had it easy. Simon was born in Vitoria in 1997, grew up in the village of Murgia and joined Athletic's academy in 2011, aged 14.

In 2018 Athletic sold Kepa Arrizabalaga to Chelsea, and Simon, a young goalkeeper out of Basconia and Bilbao Athletic, who had been sent on loan to Elche, became first choice almost by accident.

An injury to the number two Iago Herrerin, and the refusal of Alejandro Remiro to renew his contract, brought Simon back to Bilbao after only 20 days at Elche.

Many thought he would be a temporary solution. He made the position his own, and a year later he won the Under-21 European Championship with Spain. The coach? Luis de la Fuente.

His game has grown as well. Luis Enrique saw he could play with his feet and was patient with him, and Simon says the rest took a lot of analysis and training and a bit of courage.

There were doubts along the way. During the last Nations League, even De la Fuente said Simon had been badly treated for a long time, and the coach kept picking him.

Now Simon has been voted the best. He collected 351 points in the Ballon d'Or voting and finished 128 ahead of Raya in second place, with Thibaut Courtois third. Two years ago he had come second to Emi Martinez with 213 points, and last year he was not among the 10 nominees.

By his own account he is shy with people he does not know. He says he likes to "stay away from the hustle and bustle", yet friends and neighbours back home say he is the opposite with the people he does know.

He has no social media account any more, because he read everything written about him and let it decide how he felt, terrible after the bad comments and brilliant after the good ones.

The choice that explains the rest came in 2024. Simon signed a contract to 2029 with no release clause and said he wanted to be the best goalkeeper in the world as part of Athletic.

"I owe the life I have to Athletic," he said. Athletic's Basque-only policy means there is no Champions League every year and individual awards are difficult to get. But now he is the first Spanish goalkeeper to win the Yashin Trophy.

When he was small there was no drinking water in his village, and he often helped his grandparents fill the jugs from the water tanker.

On one of his latest visits, he arrived in the car he has driven for eight years, gathered all the village children and took them for a kickabout.

That is what he did with his biggest night: he gave it away to others.

Do you still think that the boy who used to tear his trousers diving on dirt pitches and on asphalt, to his mother's despair, does not deserve the prize?

articles.title: Japan stun Brazil 3-2 in stoppage time as Ancelotti, Raphinha sent off
articles.summary: Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s late goal helps Japan avenge their defeat by Brazil in the World Cup round of 32.
articles.body:
Brazil forward Raphinha and manager Carlo Ancelotti were shown red cards for protesting against a referee’s decision in the South American giant’s shock defeat to Japan in a thrilling friendly match in Singapore.

Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto netted his first international goal with a late winner on Saturday as Japan edged Brazil 3-2 at the National Stadium.

A brilliant brace by Vinicius Jr had erased a two-goal deficit after strikes by Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the Samurai Blue 2-0 up in the opening 19 minutes.

But Sakamoto was in the right place to fire home after latching on to Kodai Sano’s deflected effort in stoppage time to give the Asian side a dramatic victory in front of 38,688 people.

Brazil appealed for a foul in the build-up to the goal, but VAR upheld the goal, and Raphinha and manager Ancelotti were shown red cards for their protests.

Ancelotti seemed surprised at the decision while Raphinha was led away by midfielder Marlon Gomes and team officials as he tried to approach referee Jansen Foo, who was instead confronted by Vinicius and Bruno Guimaraes.

“The referee gave me a red card because he said I wasn’t able to control the bench and that all the players were on the field,” Ancelotti said at a news conference.

“It’s a shame about the result because we don’t like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many positives. Some players who played for the first time showed good quality. For 70 minutes, the team played well.

“The result, obviously, was influenced by the referee’s performance, … but it’s not his fault. It was a high-level match, and I don’t think he had the experience to handle this kind of game.”

Raphinha was still fuming over the “unacceptable” red card as he critiqued the referee’s decisions while speaking to reporters after the match.

“First of all, I’d like to take this opportunity to apologise for my behaviour and for being sent off,” Raphinha said.

“Sometimes it’s hard to keep calm, especially after what I felt were so many refereeing errors during the match. I tried to speak to him several times, and not once did I feel he was open to discussion. I believe that he made many errors throughout the game, and that is unacceptable,” the Brazil captain said.

“In my view, their first goal involved a foul when the opponent took the ball off me with his hand. I think it’s a foul, but I can understand why it wasn’t given based on the current law. Then there was the penalty in the first half. In my opinion, it was a penalty, but he said no.

“Then, for their third goal, there was a clear foul on Joao Gomes. With the help of VAR, he eventually allowed the goal. It’s very difficult not to talk about the refereeing.”

The victory carried added significance for Japan, who suffered a heartbreaking exit to Brazil in the World Cup last 32 in June. On that occasion, Gabriel Martinelli struck in stoppage time to complete a 2-1 comeback win for the South Americans.

“I’m happy that I can say that today’s match was the best match in my eight-year tenure,” Japan head coach Hajime Moriyasu said after the game.

“Brazil’s intensity went up once we took the lead, and it was all about what we could do then.

“Our players performed at the world’s top standard. These wins lead to victories at the World Cup, and I hope they continue to do the same,” Moriyasu added.

The 58-year-old is expected to step down after a friendly against Paraguay on Tuesday and said he is looking forward to handing over to successor Go Oiwa.

“Now I need to pass the baton to the next coach, and that’s all I am focusing on.”

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 11
articles.summary: The Week 11 college football slate lacked a headlining upset, but that doesn't mean there's not plenty of movement in the Top 25 rankings due in large part to a growing list of four-loss SEC teams.
articles.body:
The Week 11 college football slate lacked a headlining upset, but that doesn't mean there's not plenty of movement in the Top 25 rankings due in large part to a growing list of four-loss SEC teams.

South Carolina and LSU both took their fourth loss of the year, while Kentucky, USC, Houston and SMU suffered their third defeat, opening the door for some Group of Six teams to sneak into the back of the rankings.

The Saturday slate saved the best for last, as Utah snuck out a 40-39 victory over Arizona to avoid its first loss of the season.

Ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 11 action.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. North Texas (35-16) Next Week: at UAB

The Roadrunners were pushing for a spot in the AP Top 25 before suffering a 60-29 loss on the road against Florida Atlantic in Week 10, as their only other defeat had come against Texas during nonconference play. They bounced back from that second loss with a quality win against a North Texas squad that also entered the game with a 7-2 record. A'Marion Peterson (11 carries, 179 yards, 4 TD) accounted for all of UTSA's offensive touchdowns, while the defense forced two turnovers and returned an interception for a score.

Week 11 Result: WIN at South Florida (52-41) Next Week: at Navy

Marcus Stokes had 313 passing yards, 73 rushing yards and five total touchdowns, and the Tigers finished strong after blowing a 21-0 lead to reach eight wins for the fourth consecutive season. Stokes now has 38 total touchdowns on the year as one of the most productive transfer quarterbacks in the country after playing at West Florida last season. The Tigers lost to Boise State and Tulane on the road, but have built one of the better Group of Six resumes in the country.

Week 11 Result: LOSS at Colorado (32-42) Next Week: at West Virginia

The Cougars led 20-7 in the first half on Friday against Colorado, but the Buffaloes responded with 28 unanswered points en route to an upset victory. Houston quarterback Conner Weigman had an interception and a lost fumble in one of his worst individual performances of the season, though he still had 272 passing yards and three touchdowns. It's hard to see a path to the College Football Playoff for a three-loss Big 12 team.

Week 11 Result: WIN at North Carolina (16-14) Next Week: vs. Pittsburgh

The Cardinals had two field goals and a touchdown on their first three offensive possessions, then had four punts and a missed field goal on their next five drives as both offenses stalled and it was a 13-7 game early in the fourth quarter. A 10-play, 60-yard drive that ended in a field goal made it a 16-7 score with 7:28 remaining, and that ended up being the game-winning score after a late North Carolina touchdown made things interesting. With a 6-2 record in ACC play, they sit third in the conference standings behind Miami and Wake Forest.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. MTSU (28-23) Next Week: vs. Western Kentucky

The Flames pounded out 53 carries for 370 yards and three touchdowns, with Kam Davis (20 carries, 126 yards, 1 TD) and Jaylon Coleman (7 carries, 84 yards, 1 TD) leading the charge. They have now won nine straight since dropping their season opener on the road against James Madison, and are undefeated in Conference USA play. If Boise State falters, Liberty looks like the next team up in the Group of Six conversation after New Mexico lost on Saturday.

Week 11 Result: at Oklahoma on Sunday Next Week: vs. Wofford

The Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma game was delayed until Sunday after the SEC postponed the game due to the FAA ground stop on Friday. The Rebels are looking to bounce back from a 42-7 steamrolling at the hands of Georgia in Week 10, which marked their second loss in three games and effectively eliminated them from the playoff conversation. Trinidad Chambliss has 2,359 passing yards and 18 touchdowns, but he has also thrown an SEC-high nine interceptions, including five in his last three games.

Week 11 Result: LOSS vs. Utah (39-40) Next Week: at Kansas State

Noah Fifita had 356 passing yards and three touchdowns, and the Wildcats led 39-33 with 3:13 remaining after he hit Isaiah Mizell with a 10-yard scoring strike, but Utah answered with a go-ahead score to avoid the upset. Arizona's resume now featured losses to BYU, Texas Tech and Utah by a combined 20 points, as they have been competitive in every game they've played this year.

Week 11 Result: LOSS at Indiana (13-27) Next Week: vs. Maryland

Jayden Maiava threw three interceptions, including two in the fourth quarter, and the Trojans managed just one touchdown in five trips to the red zone. Waymond Jordan (13 carries, 51 yards) and King Miller (12 carries, 47 yards) were unable to pick up the slack in the running game. The Trojans entered the game still eyeing a potential path to the College Football Playoff, but a third loss almost certainly dashes those hopes.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Northwestern (28-19) Next Week: at Nebraska

After back-to-back losses to USC and Oregon, the Buckeyes beat a good Northwestern team on Saturday behind a strong showing from the Luke Faley-to-Jeremiah Smith connection. Ohio State's true freshman quarterback has taken some time to settle in since replacing the injured Julian Sayin, but he threw for 201 yards and three touchdowns, with Smith hauling in 11 catches for 117 yards and a score. Bo Jackson added 20 carries for 114 yards and a touchdown to lead the rushing attack, while the Wildcats were limited to 29 carries for 53 yards.

Week 11 Result: LOSS vs. Florida (14-21) Next Week: at Missouri

The Wildcats ripped off a 15-play, 86-yard touchdown drive on their first possession of the game, but that ended up accounting for half their points and a sizable chunk of their 242 total yards. The Kentucky defense had a tough time containing quarterback Aaron Philo, who finished with 102 rushing yards. Meanwhile, the Wildcats as a team managed just 61 yards on 27 carries. With back-to-back losses, Kentucky has slipped out of the College Football Playoff picture after debuting at No. 6 in the first CFP rankings.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Michigan (31-7) Next Week: at Michigan State

Dylan Raiola threw for a season-high 341 yards and four touchdowns in his best game since taking over for an injured Dante Moore at quarterback, and the Ducks have won three straight after briefly falling out of the national picture. The Oregon defense had two takeaways and forced five punts and three turnovers on downs while essentially relegating the Michigan offense to run only as the Wolverines were 6-of-20 passing for 71 yards.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Purdue (28-7) Next Week: at Illinois

L.J. Phillips Jr. had 23 carries for 123 yards to lead the Hawkeyes rushing attack, while Hank Brown tallied 220 total yards with a passing touchdown and a rushing touchdown. That was more than enough offensive production backed by a defense that forced seven empty possessions as Purdue had a turnover, three punts, two turnovers on downs and a missed field goal. Iowa has now outscored the opposition by an impressive 82-17 margin during its current three-game winning streak.

13. Boise State (9-1, Previous Rank: 14)

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Oregon State (46-41) Next Week: vs. San Diego State

Quarterback Maddux Madsen returned after missing Week 10 with a knee injury and threw for 371 yards and four touchdowns in a shootout as both teams eclipsed 500 total yards of offense. The bulk of that production went to Rasean Jones (11 catches, 230 yards, 3 TD), as the passing attack stepped up in a game where Dylan Riley (14 carries, 50 yards) and a rushing attack averaging 237.1 yards per game was held in check.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Baylor (28-7) Next Week: at Kansas

Bear Bachmeier had three first-half rushing touchdowns, then capped off the scoring with a passing touchdown in the fourth quarter as BYU avoided picking up a third loss to stay alive in the College Football Playoff picture. Defensively, the Cougars' secondary held Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway below 200 passing yards for the first time this season while allowing just 238 total yards of offense. Is the victory over Notre Dame enough to prop up their CFP resume if they don't make the Big 12 championship game?

Week 11 Result: WIN at Oklahoma State (52-27) Next Week: at Baylor

In his third start since replacing Will Hammond as Texas Tech's starting quarterback, Thomas Castellanos had 263 passing yards and four touchdowns to lead the Red Raiders to a lopsided victory. J'Koby Williams (19 carries, 124 yards, 1 TD) helped open up the passing game with a stellar performance on the ground, and the Texas Tech defense also deserves a ton of credit for holding Drew Mestemaker below 300 passing yards for the first time since Week 1 while picking him off twice.

10. Wake Forest (9-1, Previous Rank: 10)

Week 11 Result: WIN at SMU (49-7) Next Week: at Georgia Tech

In a game where they were just 1.5-point favorites, the Demon Deacons built a 42-0 halftime lead and cruised to victory over SMU. The Wake Forest offense piled up 535 total yards, including 286 rushing yards and 6.4 yards per carry. Gio Lopez had 201 passing yards, 34 rushing yards and three total touchdowns in his return from injury, while the defense forced three turnovers and two turnovers on downs in a dominant all-around performance.

Week 11 Result: WIN at Vanderbilt (21-6) Next Week: vs. Chattanooga

The Crimson Tide took control of the game with consecutive touchdown drives to start the second half, turning a 7-3 game into a comfortable 21-6 advantage. Keelon Russell had three passing touchdowns, and Alabama overcame two turnovers thanks to a stellar performance from the defense. Vanderbilt finished with 235 total yards, including 12 rushing yards on 23 carries, and went just 2-for-15 on third-down conversions. A cupcake against Chattanooga next week will serve as a reset before the annual Iron Bowl.

Week 11 Result: WIN at Texas A&M (22-7) Next Week: vs. LSU

The Volunteers defense shined once again as they improved to 5-2 in SEC play and kept their SEC championship game hopes alive. The Aggies were held to just 179 total yards and eight first downs, as the Tennessee defense came up with two turnovers and dominated the game from start to finish. DeSean Bishop (34 carries, 97 yards) and Javin Gordon (11 carries, 78 yards) shouldered the load offensively, and Cooper Ranvier nailed all five of his field goal attempts.

Week 11 Result: WIN at LSU (22-21) Next Week: vs. Arkansas

The Longhorns drove 58 yards on 12 plays in just over two minutes for the game-winning touchdown, as Arch Manning found Raleek Brown for a four-yard touchdown strike with two seconds remaining for a comeback win. In a game where both quarterbacks threw three interceptions, Texas trailed 21-10 midway through the third quarter. However, the Longhorns scored the final 12 points of the game to pull out the win and potentially seal their spot in the College Football Playoff if they can avoid an upset down the stretch.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. USC (27-13) Next Week: at Washington

A healthy Josh Hoover was relegated to the bench in favor of Grant Wilson at quarterback, and he finished with 305 passing yards and two touchdowns while averaging an impressive 11.3 yards per attempt. The Indiana defense picked off Jayden Maiava three times and allowed just 2-of-11 on third-down conversions while holding the high-powered Trojans offense to one touchdown on five trips to the red zone.

5. Miami Hurricanes (9-1, Previous Rank: 5)

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Duke (36-25) Next Week: vs. Virginia Tech

Darian Mensah threw for 382 yards and a touchdown against his former team, and Miami bounced back from its first loss of the season a week ago against Notre Dame.

The Hurricanes led the entire game, but never pulled away, settling for three field goals and also punting twice as their high-powered offense was kept in check. Meanwhile, they allowed 131 rushing yards, 93 receiving yards and two touchdowns to Duke's star running back Nate Sheppard, though that was the bulk of the Blue Devils' offensive production.

With a 7-0 record in ACC play and only home games against Virginia Tech and Boston College remaining, a trip to the ACC championship game and a clear path to the College Football Playoff remain.

4. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Boston College (41-7) Next Week: vs. SMU

The Fighting Irish buried Boston College with 24 points in the second quarter en route to a 31-0 halftime lead, avoiding any letdown on the heels of last weekend's huge victory over No. 1 Miami.

Jonaz Walton (15 carries, 141 yards, 1 TD) and Nolan James Jr. (14 carries, 73 yards, 1 TD) helped the Notre Dame running game average 6.9 yards per carry, while the defensive front limited the Eagles to 2.6 yards per rush attempt on the other side of the ball.

Next week's game against SMU has a little less juice after the Mustangs were steamrolled by Wake Forest on Saturday, but the Fighting Irish have already made their College Football Playoff case with the Miami win.

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Illinois (22-14) Next Week: at Michigan

The Bruins were squarely on upset alert when quarterback Ty Dieffenbach exited Friday night's game in the second quarter with an elbow injury, but he returned after halftime and led a pair of fourth quarter scoring drives to keep UCLA's undefeated season intact.

Dieffenbach, who is already starting in place of the injured Nico Iamaleava, finished with 232 passing yards and two touchdowns. The Bruins leaned on the passing game as they managed just 3.2 yards per carry on the ground.

The UCLA defense had three interceptions and limited Katin Houser to 4.8 yards per attempt en route to just 240 yards of total offense for the Fighting Illini.

Week 11 Result: WIN at Arizona (40-39) Next Week: at TCU

Devon Dampier threw the go-ahead 70-yard touchdown pass to Creed Whittemore with 2:35 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Utes defense forced a three-and-out on the ensuing Arizona possession to survive a thrilling shootout on the road.

The Utes led 33-28 early in the fourth quarter, but the Wildcats responded with a field goal, a forced punt and a touchdown to take a 39-33 lead with 3:13 left, setting the stage for Dampier's deep strike to retake the lead.

Dampier finished with 204 passing yards, 100 rushing yards and four total touchdowns, while Daniel Bray pounded out 18 carries for 197 yards and a score in what was the toughest remaining test for Utah in pursuit of an undefeated regular season. TCU and West Virginia are all that stands in the way.

1. Georgia Bulldogs (9-1, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 11 Result: WIN vs. Missouri (48-21) Next Week: at South Carolina

The Bulldogs scored the first 24 points of the game and built a 31-7 lead heading into halftime, cruising to victory against a ranked opponent to improve to 7-1 in SEC play and maintain their status as the conference's top dog.

Gunner Stockton (18/24, 252 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT, rush TD) had an efficient game under center, while Nate Frazier (14 carries, 72 yards, 3 TD) and Dwight Phillips Jr. (7 carries, 66 yards) shined against a Missouri run defense that entered the week 13th in the nation with 95.8 rushing yards allowed per game.

A road game against South Carolina and a home matchup with in-state rival Georgia Tech are all that stands between Georgia and a trip to the SEC championship game and the potential No. 1 seed in the College Football Playoff.

articles.title: Why has Arsenal not opened contract talks with Odegaard?
articles.summary: Martin Odegaard remains one of the most important players in the Arsenal squad and has continued to demonstrate his value to the team this season.Injuries di...
articles.body:
Martin Odegaard remains one of the most important players in the Arsenal squad and has continued to demonstrate his value to the team this season.

Injuries disrupted his previous campaign and affected the contribution he could make to the Gunners' success. Arsenal were therefore keen to see their captain return to full fitness and rediscover his best form.

He remained fit during the World Cup in the summer, as Norway impressed, and has continued to perform well for Arsenal this season. His return to regular action has been encouraging, although speculation about his long-term future at the Emirates has also emerged.

Odegaard is Arsenal captain for a reason and has repeatedly shown that he can be trusted to deliver when called upon. The club regard him as one of their leading players, but questions remain about his contract situation.

Despite reports suggesting that discussions over a new deal are underway, Arsenal have yet to open formal talks with the midfielder. That has created some uncertainty about his future, particularly given his importance to Mikel Arteta's plans.

The Gunners will want to keep their captain for as long as possible, especially after seeing how much his absence affected the team last season. However, securing his long-term future will require both sides to reach an agreement.

Odegaard is currently away with Norway during the international break, and he was asked about the situation. His response did not provide the positive update Arsenal supporters might have hoped for.

Odegaard provides update on contract situation

Speaking via TV2 , the midfielder admitted that there have not been many discussions about a new agreement and confirmed that negotiations have not started.

"We haven't talked about it much," Odegaard said.

"First and foremost, the focus is now on what's happening on the pitch, so everyone knows the situation around.

"I'm happy and hope I can be there for a long time to come, but so far we haven't started on that."

His comments suggest that Odegaard remains happy at Arsenal and would welcome a lengthy stay at the club. However, the absence of formal talks means there is still work to be done before his future is secured.

For now, the captain's priority remains performing on the pitch, while Arsenal will hope to begin discussions and reach an agreement that keeps one of their most important players at the Emirates.

articles.title: KU basketball limits Kentucky’s Milan Momcilovic, plus more takeaways
articles.summary: KU basketball limited one of the best 3-point shooters in the nation during the Champions Classic win vs Kentucky. Here’s how, plus more takeaways.
articles.body:
CHICAGO — While Kentucky forward Milan Momcilovic entered the Champions Classic matchup Tuesday, Nov. 10, against Kansas as a 3-point threat, by game's end his stat-line didn't resemble anything like it.

Momcilovic, a senior, finished with just five points while shooting 2-for-7 from the field and 1-for-3 from behind the arc. He wasn't the factor he could have been offensively, in what ended up being an 89-69 loss against No. 14 KU in Chicago. And Kansas coach Bill Self, well aware of Momcilovic due to Momcilovic's time previously at Iowa State, praised his team's defensive effort on Momcilovic postgame.

According to Self, the plan was to get there on catch, so the Jayhawks could take away Momcilovic's ability to get off a quality look before Momcilovic was even in a position to take one. KU also wanted to limit the number of 3s Momcilovic would attempt, with Self volunteering the goal was four. So, that Momcilovic only took three, is about as good as Self could hope for.

KU senior guard Tre White acknowledged it wasn't easy to contain Momcilovic and described it as a team effort. Jayhawks fifth-year forward Trey Kaufman-Renn praised how the guards stepped up defensively, considering senior guard Melvin Council Jr. is out due to injury right now. Kaufman-Renn also pointed out that in the first half, Momcilovic didn't even take an attempt from behind the arc.

Here are a few more takeaways from this win for Kansas (3-0):

While Kansas won this game by 20 points and led by as many as 23, it's not as if things started off well for the Jayhawks. Not long into the first half, they were down 10-5 against the Wildcats. It led Self to call a timeout.

Self explained Kentucky was getting anything it wanted offensively, and KU had come into the game wanting to be physical and not give up easy baskets. From Self's perspective, it was like his team was nervous to guard the Wildcats. But after that point, while Kentucky did miss some shots it would usually hit, he thought his Jayhawks guarded pretty well.

Kansas dominates in points off of turnovers

There were some individual performances from Kansas that certainly stood out. White scored a career-high 30 points, freshman guard Tyran Stokes stood out with a 23-point and 10-rebound double-double and Kaufman-Renn had 12 points, six rebounds and six assists. But there's a team statistic that KU dominated, that sticks out as well.

Kansas finished the game with 22 points off of 15 Kentucky turnovers, while the Wildcats never scored any points off of 10 Jayhawks turnovers. Self acknowledged he probably would have never seen a 22-0 advantage like that coming while noting a lot of that is luck. What he thought about KU's performance in that regard, was when it did turn the ball over it was in a position where the Jayhawks could at least get back in transition.

Trey Kaufman-Renn continues to make the game easier for his teammates

Kaufman-Renn was a late addition to the KU roster ahead of the regular season and one who arrived with a lot of potential. But if anyone thought he might need some time to acclimate, it seems he's doing just fine for himself already. And if there are greater heights he can reach, that only bodes well for the Jayhawks.

Stokes detailed, when discussing how Kaufman-Renn makes the game easier for his teammates, that Kaufman-Renn helps space the floor well and is great in short-roll situations. You can give Kaufman-Renn the ball, and the defense will gravitate toward him. The experience Kaufman-Renn has in college is something Stokes feels is a benefit for himself, because Kaufman-Renn has the ability to get him the ball even when he doesn't think he's open.

articles.title: Felipe VI presidirá el España-Inglaterra en el Metropolitano
articles.standfirst: Casa Real ha confirmado la presencia del monarca español en el palco del estadio atlético
articles.summary: Casa Real ha confirmado la presencia del monarca español en el palco del estadio atlético
articles.body: España e Inglaterra ponen el broche final a un año mundialista en un escenario de máxima exigencia para medir sus fuerzas. El Metropolitano acoge el duelo entre dos de las grandes potencias actuales, dos estilos que dominan el fútbol de hoy y que van a dirimir el liderato del grupo A3 de la Liga de Naciones. La vigente campeona del mundo se mide a una selección inglesa, subcampeona de Europa, y consolidada en la élite gracias a una generación de estrellas mundiales. Un choque mayúsculo, el mejor del último parón internacional de 2026. Un duelo que estará presidido por el Rey de España, Felipe VI. Casa Real ha confirmado que el palco de autoridades del estadio del Atlético de Madrid contará con la presencia del monarca español. Don Felipe suele acompañar a la Selección Española de Fútbol y a todo el deporte español en muchas de sus finales y éxitos. En la pasada Eurocopa de 2024, acompañó a la Roja en los partidos clave, así como en la final ante Inglaterra, en la que se terminó conquistando el título. En el último Mundial de Estados Unidos, el Rey Felipe VI acudió con toda la Familia Real a New Jersey para presenciar la final ante Argentina que terminó suponiendo la segunda estrella para el combinado nacional. Hoy, en el último gran partido del año para España, el monarca presidirá el palco de autoridades.

articles.title: Official: Mancini drops four players for Belgium vs. Italy, Cisse and Liberali called up
articles.summary: Roberto Mancini has decided which members of his squad will have to watch Sunday’s decisive Nations League clash between Belgium and Italy from the stands, a...
articles.body:
Roberto Mancini has decided which members of his squad will have to watch Sunday's decisive Nations League clash between Belgium and Italy from the stands, and has also decided to include Alphadjo Cisse and Mattia Liberali in his matchday squad this time around.

Italy are in Brussels to take on Belgium in their final match of the Nations League group stage on Sunday evening (19.45 GMT). The Azzurri lead the group ahead of kick-off having defeated France 3-1 in San Siro on Thursday night.

Ahead of kick-off this evening, Italy lead the group on 10 points, leading France on goal difference and head-to-head, Belgium are in third place on nine points and Turkey are in last on zero.

MILAN – NOVEMBER 12: Pio Esposito of Italy celebrates scoring his team's third goal with teammates during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images)

Belgium were the victors when they took on the Azzurri in Rome in the first round of group stage fixtures at the beginning of the September-October international break.

As is customary for Nations League group stage fixtures, Mancini must whittle down his roster to a matchday squad of 23 players, three of whom must be goalkeepers.

Mancini confirmed on Saturday that Italy will be without two of their starters from the France game as Davide Frattesi and Nicolo Cambiaghi have not recovered. They have not been included in Sunday's matchday squad.

MILAN – NOVEMBER 12: Sebastiano Esposito of Italy misses from the penalty spot during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images)

It has since been confirmed that Sebastiano Esposito will be left out of Sunday's squad to face Belgium, as will Samuele Ricci, Federico Gatti and Matteo Palma. Gatti and Palma were also left out against France.

Meanwhile, Cisse, Liberali, Honest Ahanor and Niccolo Pisilli have been called up to the squad to face Belgium, having been left out against France earlier this week.

MILAN – NOVEMBER 12: Roberto Mancini, Head Coach of Italy, gestures during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images)

Goalkeepers: Marco Carnesecchi, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Guglielmo Vicario.

Defenders: Honest Ahanor, Alessandro Bastoni, Riccardo Calafiori, Federico Dimarco, Daniele Ghilardi, Michael Kayode, Marco Palestra, Giorgio Scalvini.

Midfielders: Nicolo Barella, Alphadjo Cisse, Issa Doumbia, Nicolo Fagioli, Mattia Liberali, Niccolo Pisilli, Alessandro Romano, Sandro Tonali.

Forwards: Pio Esposito, Luca Koleosho, Gianluca Scamacca, Antonio Vergara.

articles.title: Ruthless Australia win record fourth Women's World Cup
articles.summary: Australia blow New Zealand away in the first half, with a hat-trick for Jaime Chapman, to win 34-10 in Brisbane and clinch a record fourth World Cup.
articles.body:
Tries: Chapman 3, Bent, Surgis, Upton Goals: Southwell 5

Jaime Chapman's grin after acrobatically diving over in the corner said it all. Her second try of the match and Australia's third – the World Cup final put to bed inside 15 minutes.

The red-hot Australian winning machine blew New Zealand away in the first half as they cantered to a record fourth World Cup title - and fourth in a row - with a 34-10 victory in Brisbane.

Making light work of the blistering conditions, which necessitated a drinks break in either half and an extended interval, the Jillaroos ran in six tries to the Kiwi Ferns' one in the opening 35 minutes, including an initial burst of 24 unanswered points and a hat-trick for Chapman.

Record books were consulted at the break, with Australia on course to challenge New Zealand's 58-0 winning margin from the 2003 final. But the two sides neutralised one another during the second period, New Zealand maintaining their record of not conceding after the break at this tournament - and bagging a consolation try - albeit with Australia long out of sight.

The undisputed dominant force in women's rugby league, Australia are now unbeaten in 16 World Cup matches - a run stretching back to July 2013.

Aside from a brief first-half scare against Fiji in the semi-finals, who became the first side for 13 years to open the scoring in a World Cup game against Australia, it has been a serene procession to the title, scoring 306 points while conceding just 30.

It was a ruthless first-half performance from the Jillaroos, who capitalised on the field position presented by a succession of errors and ill-discipline from New Zealand- combined with some sluggish defending – for their opening three tries.

Chapman overpowered three defenders on the left wing to open the scoring after just 125 seconds and produced a flying finish from a sharp offload in the same area after Shaylee Bent had sliced through New Zealand's defence from close range for Australia's second.

After Jess Sergis went the length of the field for their fourth, albeit with a suspected forward pass in the build-up, Shannon Mato dived over as New Zealand profited from back-to-back infringements from the hosts.

However, normal service quickly resumed, with Chapman evading multiple tackles as she ran 60 metres to complete her hat-trick before slick handling down the right wing allowed Abbi Church to feed Tamika Upton on her inside for a simple score under the posts.

Head coach Jess Skinner's decision to select Jesse Southwell ahead of Jocelyn Kelleher at stand-off paid off, as she nonchalantly kicked five of her six conversions, including two from the left touchline.

But this was undeniably Chapman's show, with the 24-year-old, who has faced a succession of injuries, including a spinal fracture in February 2025, and media attention on her personal life, named player of the match.

"She's so young - it's quite scary," said captain Isabelle Kelly. "As a centre, your job is to provide for your winger. Every single time she's there, she executes and finishes to such a high standard.

"The fact she was able to get that down with three girls on her is incredible. Once you get her strides going, she's very hard to stop.

"She's had a lot of stuff going on the last few years and she's really stepped up and owned that position."

Australia went completely off the boil in the second half, with Tarryn Aiken - denied by a try-saving tackle from Georgia Hale - producing their only scoring opportunity of note.

New Zealand, to their credit, vastly improved when defending on the front foot but remained frustrating in attack, completing barely half of their sets due to repeated handling errors, loose passing, and a consistent failure to feed stand-off Chantay Kiria-Ratu.

Mackenzie Wiki's 70th minute try was a deserved, if futile, reward for their second-half efforts.

"Mixed emotions - we obviously came with high hopes of playing really well," said New Zealand head coach Ricky Henry.

"It was a game of two halves and that's the frustrating part for us. We were able to get it back together in the second half but it was too little, too late.

"We didn't handle the speed of the game at the start. They got on top and from there, we couldn't regroup and get our rhythm."

Matt's player of the match: Jaime Chapman

Whether it's stealing the show at the Dally M awards or racking up World Cup final hat-tricks, Jaime Chapman simply takes the spotlight every time.

This was a display that highlighted everything good about rugby league; her first try was brute strength, the second showed spectacular athleticism to cartwheel over to score and the hat-trick try was all about sheer pace, burning off flailing attempts from her pursuers to halt her progress.

She threw in a try-saver to boot, on top of 151 metres, three line-breaks and seven tackle-busts.

Chapman is already a superstar within her sport. This performance ought to be the springboard to something more. World-class athlete and marketable talent.

articles.title: Lopetegui no seguirá con Qatar tras el aplazamiento de la Copa Asia
articles.standfirst: El retraso del torneo varía los planes de futuro y el técnico español no renovará su contrato, que finaliza en abril de 2027
articles.summary: El retraso del torneo varía los planes de futuro y el técnico español no renovará su contrato, que finaliza en abril de 2027
articles.body: Julen Lopetegui (Asteasu, 1966) no es ajeno a la particular situación socio-política que se vive en Oriente Medio. La decisión de aplazar la Copa Asia un año, hasta enero de 2028, por los ataques que ha sufrido Arabia Saudí por parte de los rebeldes hutíes del Yemen ha motivado que el técnico español se replantee su futuro. El 'horizonte' con el que firmó hace casi dos años ha cambiado por completo y entiende que ha cubierto su ciclo en Doha. De ahí que tenga decidido no continuar al frente de Qatar más allá de abril de 2027, una vez finalice su contrato. Es cierto que aún no se ha sentado con la Federación para cerrar el acuerdo sobre su salida, pero se trata de una decisión madurada después del Mundial y la disputa de la Copa del Golfo... y acentuada por el aplazamiento de la Copa Asia. No es una reacción en caliente o una estrategia de mercado. Por la cabeza de Lopetegui no pasa coger ningún equipo a mitad de temporada. De hecho, ha tenido propuestas después de la Copa del Mundo que no ha atendido por su compromiso con Qatar. Su idea es coger un proyecto de nivel cuando finalice su contrato, pero ya con vistas a la temporada 2027-28. Su foco, ahora mismo, está en el amistoso del martes contra Corea del Sur, último encuentro de este 2026 tras la suspensión del amistoso de diciembre frente a Arabia Saudí. Ya sólo quedarán por delante los duelos de la ventana internacional de marzo de 2027. El exseleccionador español confía en poner fin de la mejor manera posible a lo que considera una experiencia vital y deportiva muy positiva en Doha. Cabe recordar que llegó a Qatar en una situación complicada -venía de encadenar cuatro derrotas seguidas y con el play-off casi imposible- y se convirtió en el primer seleccionador en clasificar al país para una Copa del Mundo por méritos propios, ya que en 2022 ejercieron de anfitriones, al ganar a Emiratos en una repesca celebrada como un éxito en el país. "La vida me debía un Mundial", aseguró Lopetegui, que logró otro hito histórico. El empate ante Suiza (1-1) otorgó a Qatar su primer punto en una Copa del Mundo. No sólo eso. También alcanzó las semifinales de la Copa del Golfo, donde acabó perdiendo, por penaltis, ante Arabia Saudí, anfitriona y, a la postre, campeona. Ahora, sin embargo, con el aplazamiento de la Copa Asia es hora de cambiar de rumbo una vez finalice el contrato actual.
